# Upcoming features

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/project/roadmap

# Upcoming features

What is planned or under development after the first release. The list is written at the release of ver. 1.0.0.

Several components in one potential, and tracers in a fixed potential: the package’s results, stages and files
are shaped per component already; what is to be written is the theory.

The \(N\)-body test problem of the isolation runs of Chiang+(2026d) as a
GAMER test problem, with its analysis scripts.


---

# Accuracy tables

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/accuracy

# Accuracy tables

The accuracy grid is a fixed set of models, four tables of rows by columns, run unchanged at every release. Each
model’s distribution function is inverted and its density \(\varrho_{\rm inv}\) computed back from it; the
roundtrip error \(|(\varrho_{\rm inv} - \varrho)/\varrho|\), against the input profile \(\varrho\), is read at
513 radii, and a cell gives that error over \(10^{-4} < R < 10^{5}\) (\(R\) in scale radii):

its maximum, then its median, then the tier the result itself reports (goal: \(10^{-6}\) or less;
ceiling: \(10^{-4}\) or less; warning: \(10^{-2}\) or less; refused: beyond, see Accuracy);

refused and the refusal’s name, where the package refuses the model (the full message is in the cell’s
tooltip and in the CSV);

excluded where the anisotropy breaks the cusp bound \(\gamma \ge 2\beta_{\rm c}\) (computed, and recorded in the
CSV). A Type II model without a truncation has its distribution function only above the energy \(P(R_{\rm a})\): its
cell gives the tier the package reports over that support and the note “support above \(P(R_{\rm a})\)”, not the
density’s roundtrip, which is no measure there.

A † marks a cell whose outcome is not the one the grid expects. The tables are at the default tier; the CSV holds
every range the grid reads, the radius of each maximum and the compute times. The tables of earlier releases are
on Accuracy by release.

The grid of ver. 0.9.9, run at d59731fb, whose numerical code is 52a0ef0b’s (cpu), the default tier: the full grid as CSV and its member list.

# Velocity anisotropy

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/anisotropy

# Velocity anisotropy

Module pianistpy.anisotropy

Velocity anisotropy models.

class pianistpy.anisotropy.Anisotropy(beta_c=0.0, r_a=inf, kind='I')

Velocity anisotropy of one component.

The isotropic, constant-anisotropy, Osipkov-Merritt (OM) and
Cuddeford-Osipkov-Merritt (COM) models are regions of the parameters of
this one class, since the COM model contains the other three.

Parameters:

beta_c (float, optional) – Central anisotropy \(\beta_{\rm c}\), smaller than 1. The default,
exactly 0, gives an isotropic or an OM model.

r_a (float, optional) – Anisotropy radius \(R_{\rm a}\) in internal units, positive. The
default, infinity, gives an isotropic or a constant-anisotropy model.

kind ({"I", "II"}, optional) – Type of the OM or COM model. Stored as "I" when r_a is
infinite, where the type does not enter the model, so that one model
has one identity.

Notes

The model is identified by exact comparison of the parameters as given:
beta_c == 0 and an infinite r_a. A value such as 1e-12 is a
constant-anisotropy model and is not rounded to zero. The package is
tested to give results that are continuous through these special values.

Examples

```
>>> Anisotropy().model
'isotropic'
>>> Anisotropy(beta_c=0.3).model
'constant'
>>> Anisotropy(r_a=10.0).model
'om'
>>> Anisotropy(beta_c=-0.25, r_a=10.0, kind="II").model
'com'

```

factor(r, xp=np)

Return the factor \(g(R)\) of the augmented density.

\(g = 1/h\), with \(h\) from inverse_factor, the package’s
one form of the factor, which the inversion, the edge law and the
Poisson solve read too.

Parameters:

r (array-like) – Radius, in internal units.

xp (module, optional) – The array namespace, NumPy by default; JAX’s inside a kernel.

Returns:

g – \(g(R)\): 1 (isotropic), \(R^{-2\beta_{\rm c}}\)
(constant), \((1 \pm R^2/R_{\rm a}^2)^{-1}\) (OM) and
\(R^{-2\beta_{\rm c}} (1 \pm R^2/R_{\rm a}^2)^{-(1-\beta_{\rm c})}\)
(COM), the upper sign for Type I.

Return type:

array

Raises:

InputError – For a Type II model at a radius at or beyond \(R_{\rm a}\),
    where it is not defined (a traced radius is not checked).

References

Chiang+(2026d), Eq. (B43) [eqn:linearity_beta_1].

property model: str

isotropic, constant, om or com.

Type:

Label of the model in Chiang+(2026d)

property domain_edge: float

The outer edge of the radii where the anisotropy is defined:
\(R_{\rm a}\) for a Type II model (its factor is real, finite and
positive only inside it), infinite otherwise.

to_dict()

Return the anisotropy as a plain dictionary.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

classmethod from_dict(record)

Build the anisotropy from its dictionary form.

Parameters:

record (Mapping[str, Any])

Return type:

Anisotropy

# Distribution functions and models

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/df

# Distribution functions and models

Module pianistpy.df

Distribution functions and equilibrium models.

class pianistpy.df.Component(profile, anisotropy=<factory>, mass=1.0, name='component')

One component of a model: a density profile with its anisotropy.

A model is a sequence of components that share one total potential. A
single component is a sequence of length one.

Given the truncated profile of another model (parent.profile) in
place of an analytic profile, the component is Method II of Chiang+(2026d):
the density of the parent in the parent’s potential, with a new
anisotropy. It is refused here where no distribution function exists
for that anisotropy at the edge of the density.

A profile with an outer slope between 2 and 3 is refused here (OUTER
SLOPE): the outer end of the inversion and its tail exponent assume
Psi ~ 1/R, which that regime does not have.

Parameters:

profile (DoublePowerLaw or TruncatedProfile) – Density profile of the component: an analytic profile, or the
truncated profile of a model of one component.

anisotropy (Anisotropy, optional) – Velocity anisotropy of the component. Isotropic by default.

mass (float, optional) – Mass of the component relative to the first component.

name (str, optional) – Label carried by the particles and the results of the component.

property unit_profile: DoublePowerLaw

The analytic profile that fixes the internal units of the component.

to_dict()

Return the component as a plain dictionary.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

classmethod from_dict(record, profile=None)

Build the component from its dictionary form.

Parameters:

record (mapping) – The dictionary form.

profile (TruncatedProfile, optional) – The profile, where the record states a truncated one: the
record identifies it and does not hold its arrays.

Return type:

Component

class pianistpy.df.DistributionFunction(components, settings, identity, grid, table, form, k_t_min, validation, timing, inversion, units=Units(system='internal', concentration=None, mass_0_msun=None, r_0_pc=None), rows=None, source='inversion', function_name=None)

Untruncated distribution functions of the components of a model.

Returned by compute_df. It is a mathematical object: it may be negative or
non-monotonic, and states where. Only a Model can be sampled or
projected.

Parameters:

components (tuple of Component) – The components the DFs belong to.

settings (Settings) – The settings the DFs were computed with.

identity (str) – Identity string of the result.

grid (EnergyGrid) – The energies of the table and their radii.

table (DfTable) – The DFs on the grid.

form (AsymptoticForm) – The analytic form of each DF beyond the ends of its table.

k_t_min (float) – Lowest admissible truncation energy; zero where every DF is
non-negative and non-decreasing. For a Type II model whose bound is
its domain edge, the next float above \(P(R_{\rm a})\), the
smallest \(\mathcal{K}_{\rm t}\) the gates admit; the truncated
model’s edge must also lie inside \(R_{\rm a}\), which the
truncation’s solve judges (TYPE II EDGE).

validation (ValidationReport) – The report of the inversion.

timing (dict of str to float) – Wall time of each stage, in seconds.

inversion (InversionRecord or None) – How the table was made; None where it was not made by an inversion
(a closed form). Every solved DF states it.

rows (InversionRows or None) – The inversion’s rows as made on its whole grid, which the truncation
reads; None where the table was not made by an inversion.

source (str) – Where the table’s values come from: "inversion" (compute_df)
or "function" (from_function).

function_name (str or None) – The __name__ of the function the table was taken from; None for
an inversion.

units (Units)

classmethod from_function(component, f, settings=None)

Return the distribution function a function of the energy gives.

A user brings a DF (a fitting function, another code’s output) and
the package certifies it against the density by its own integration.
The function is tabulated on the energy grid compute_df places for
the same component and settings, in place of the inversion’s values,
and everything after runs as for the inversion: the forms beyond the
table, the slope column, the sign report, the validation, the
identity, and the file. The table is stored, the function is not.

Parameters:

component (Component) – The component the DF belongs to, on an analytic profile.

f (callable) – f(k, depth): takes the array of the energies K (the table’s,
in internal units) and the array of their depths P_0 - K, and
returns the DF at each, F and not its logarithm. The depth is
the grid’s own P_0 - K of each node, exact, so a fit written in
the depth near the center reads it directly; a function of K
alone may ignore it.

settings (Settings, optional) – Numerical settings. The default tier if omitted.

Returns:

df – Its source is "function" and its function_name the
function’s __name__. The table has no derivative column, and
the report’s slope_column states that it is not judged. It
has no inversion record and no rows, so truncate refuses it.

Return type:

DistributionFunction

Raises:

InputError – If the function is not finite somewhere on the grid (the first
    such K is stated), returns another shape, or the component is
    built on a tabulated profile.

property is_physical: bool

Whether the untruncated DFs are a valid equilibrium as they stand.

property diverges_at_zero: tuple[bool, ...]

Whether the DF of each component diverges as the energy goes to zero.

See AsymptoticForm.diverges_at_zero.

to(system, concentration=None, mass_0=None, r_0=None, r_vir=None)

Return the same result presented in another unit system.

The numbers of the result are not recomputed: they stay in internal
units, and what is computed from the result inherits its units.

Parameters:

system ({"internal", "model", "physical"}) – The target unit system.

concentration (float, optional) – Concentration that defines M_0, the mass inside that many scale
radii. Taken from the truncation where it was given there.

mass_0 (float or astropy Quantity, optional) – M_0, for the physical system; a float is in solar masses.

r_0 (float or astropy Quantity, optional) – The scale radius, or the concentration radius in its place, for
the physical system; a float is in parsecs.

r_vir (float or astropy Quantity, optional) – The scale radius, or the concentration radius in its place, for
the physical system; a float is in parsecs.

Returns:

df

Return type:

DistributionFunction

write(path, overwrite=False)

Write the result to a file; pianistpy.read reads it back.

Parameters:

path (str | PathLike)

overwrite (bool)

Return type:

None

write_text(path, overwrite=False)

Write the DF table as fixed-width text, an export beside the file.

One row per node of each component’s support: the energy k (in
units of the central potential, internal units), log10_df and
the slope dlog10_df_dlnk of the table, and with more than one
component its index in a component column. The header names the
result, its components and the units. The file is read back and
compared with what was written, to the digits written
(pianistpy.io.write_table).

Parameters:

path (str | PathLike)

overwrite (bool)

Return type:

None

class pianistpy.df.Model(components, truncation, settings, identity, parent, table, form, profile, validation, timing, r_trust, inversion, units=Units(system='internal', concentration=None, mass_0_msun=None, r_0_pc=None))

A valid equilibrium: truncated or untruncated, of one or more components.

Returned by truncate and solve. A model always has non-negative,
non-decreasing DFs. Whether its density ends at a finite radius is a
property of the model, spatially_finite.

Parameters:

components (tuple of Component) – The components of the model.

truncation (Truncation or None) – The truncation, or None for an untruncated model.

settings (Settings) – The settings the model was computed with.

identity (str) – Identity string of the result.

parent (str) – Identity string of the DistributionFunction the model was built from.

table (DfTable) – The DFs of the model.

form (AsymptoticForm) – The analytic form of each DF beyond the ends of its table.

profile (TruncatedProfile) – The self-consistent profile of the model.

validation (ValidationReport) – The report of the model.

timing (dict of str to float) – Wall time of each stage, in seconds.

r_trust (mapping of str to float) – The radius within which the model holds each accuracy tier, keyed by
the report’s tier names (“goal”, “ceiling”; “limit” where it is
computed): where the result is valid, not an error of it. Every tier
or none: the radii are measured on an untruncated model, from the
offset of its potential at large radii, and the mapping is empty on
a truncated model (a spatially finite one holds its table to its
edge) and where that offset is undefined. A tier the table’s first
outer row already misses has radius 0; infinite on a closed form.

inversion (InversionRecord or None) – How the model’s table was made; None where it was not made by an
inversion (a closed form). Every solved model states it.

units (Units)

property spatially_finite: bool

Whether the density reaches zero at a finite radius and mass.

property diverges_at_zero: tuple[bool, ...]

Whether the DF of each component diverges as the energy goes to zero.

See AsymptoticForm.diverges_at_zero. Such a model is a valid
equilibrium with a finite density; its DF is not monotonic.

to(system, concentration=None, mass_0=None, r_0=None, r_vir=None)

Return the same model presented in another unit system.

The numbers of the model are not recomputed: they stay in internal
units, and what is computed from the model inherits its units.

Parameters:

system ({"internal", "model", "physical"}) – The target unit system.

concentration (float, optional) – Concentration that defines M_0, the mass inside that many scale
radii. Taken from the truncation where it was given there.

mass_0 (float or astropy Quantity, optional) – M_0, for the physical system; a float is in solar masses.

r_0 (float or astropy Quantity, optional) – The scale radius, or the concentration radius in its place, for
the physical system; a float is in parsecs.

r_vir (float or astropy Quantity, optional) – The scale radius, or the concentration radius in its place, for
the physical system; a float is in parsecs.

Returns:

model

Return type:

class pianistpy.df.Truncation(k_t=None, mass_t=None, r_t=None, concentration=None)

How the distribution function of a model is truncated.

This is Method I of Chiang+(2026d). Method II needs no truncation: it is a
component whose profile is the truncated profile of another model, given
a new anisotropy.

Exactly one of k_t, mass_t and r_t is given. A target mass is given
together with the concentration that defines its unit.

Parameters:

k_t (float, optional) – Truncation energy \(\mathcal{K}_{\rm t}\), in internal units (the
central potential of the untruncated profile is 1).

mass_t (float, optional) – Target total mass of the truncated model, in MODEL units: in units of
\(M_0\), the mass of the untruncated profile inside the
concentration radius, so that a value of 1 is the virial mass. This
is the one input that is not in internal units. The truncation energy
is solved for. Requires concentration.

r_t (float, optional) – Target truncation radius \(R_{\rm t}\), in internal units (the
scale radius \(r_0\) is their unit of length). The truncation
energy is solved for.

concentration (float, optional) – Concentration \(c\) of the first component: \(M_0\) is the
mass of its untruncated profile inside \(c\,r_0\). Required
with mass_t, and refused with k_t and r_t, which do not depend
on it.

to_dict()

Return the truncation as a plain dictionary.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

classmethod from_dict(record)

Build the truncation from its dictionary form.

Parameters:

record (Mapping[str, Any])

Return type:

Truncation

truncation energy.

Parameters:

components (Component or sequence of Component) – The component of the model. This release takes one; a sequence of
several, in one total potential, is refused.

settings (Settings, optional) – Numerical settings. The default tier if omitted.

Returns:

df

    isotropic, constant beta and Osipkov-Merritt Type I).

## Gradients

Module pianistpy.df.gradient

The distribution function’s rows and table as JAX functions of the anisotropy parameters, and their Jacobians
(End-to-end differentiability).

The inversion’s gradient in the anisotropy parameters at a fixed profile.

The inversion’s rows F = T_b[g](q) (invert._rows: the kernel and the
completion below the floor) on a fixed grid q. At a fixed central anisotropy
b the operator T_b is linear in its source g, the rows of d^N rho_aux / dP^N,
so, by that linearity:

dF/dR_a    = T_b[ d_Ra g ]
dF/dbeta_c = T_b[ d_b g ] + E_b[g]

with d_theta g the mixed derivatives at fixed P (ParameterDerivs) and E_b
the derivative of the operator itself in b with g held: the prefactor C(n, b)
and the kernel’s exponent, computed by the operator at b +- d (central,
Richardson over d and d/2) or, at the corners where the inversion’s form
changes on one side (half-integer \(\beta_{\rm c}\), the pair’s switch),
by the one-sided Richardson combinations (third order) of both sides and
their mean; the step d
balances the kernel’s measured accuracy over d against the quotient’s
truncation term (_exponent_part).

The table (invert._table_pieces) is a function of the rows and of closed
forms in theta, so its derivative is the chain rule through each piece, with
every discrete choice of the forward held (the grid, the anchor, the fit’s
window, the nodes below the written floor), table_jacobian:

the rows’ log10 F and their log slope, from dF and d(dF/dK), the rows’
part as the operator’s own derivative along the mixed rows (_along);

the form above the anchor (top_patch): its least-squares fit linearized
in the rows, and the center’s exponent kappa(b) and amplitude A(b) in
closed form (the regular branch);

the nodes below the written floor (below_floor): the integral linear in
its source, the source’s cubic in (ln P, ln |g|) linearized, and in b the
floor pair’s exponent and prefactor by the same difference as E_b;

the tail (A, a(b), k), from the first node below the floor or the first
written row.

On a component on a truncated profile (Method II, tabulated.tabulated_df)
the parent is held and the child’s sources are a Leibniz sum of the parent’s
density derivatives and the factor g(R(P); beta_c, R_a), so their derivative
is the same sum with d g / d theta in closed form; the rows follow as above
on the grid held at theta, and the leaves are log10 |F| on the table’s nodes,
the edge law (p, C_0, C_1) and the center the form states, each closed form
with its derivative written out.

Served: constant beta and Cuddeford Type I (\(\beta_{\rm c}\),
\(R_{\rm a}\)), Osipkov-Merritt Type I and II (\(R_{\rm a}\)).
Refused: Cuddeford Type II, whose interior point at \(P(R_{\rm a})\) moves
with \(R_{\rm a}\) (and its exponent with \(\beta_{\rm c}\)), so the
rows of the mixed derivative are not integrable there; and a table whose
center is not on its regular branch (the critical band, where the branch
changes with \(\beta_{\rm c}\)).

pianistpy.df.gradient.inversion_nodes(component, settings)

Return the grid q the inversion places its rows on (inversion_df’s:
the pilot’s feature where the family has one, then top_limit, the
least depth at which the exact derivatives are finite in float64).

Parameters:

component (Component)

settings (Settings)

Return type:

ndarray

pianistpy.df.gradient.make_inversion_rows(component, settings, q=None)

Return (rows, params, q): rows(theta) is the inversion’s rows on
the fixed grid q as a JAX function of the component’s anisotropy
parameters (params, in that order) with a custom VJP. The forward is
invert._rows through a host callback (the forward’s numbers), the
backward the rule (rows_jacobian) at the same parameters.

Parameters:

component (Component)

settings (Settings)

q (ndarray | None)

Return type:

tuple[Any, tuple[str, …], ndarray]

pianistpy.df.gradient.make_inversion_table(component, settings, q=None)

Return (table, params, values): table(theta) is the DF table’s
values (table_jacobian’s, but the energies) as a JAX function of the
component’s anisotropy parameters with a custom VJP; values the
table at the component’s own parameters, energies included. The forward
is inversion_df’s table through a host callback, the backward the rule.
The grid and the forward’s discrete choices are those at the component’s
parameters.

Parameters:

component (Component)

settings (Settings)

q (ndarray | None)

Return type:

tuple[Any, tuple[str, …], dict[str, ndarray]]

pianistpy.df.gradient.rows_jacobian(component, settings, q=None, steps=None)

Return the inversion’s rows and their derivatives in the component’s
anisotropy parameters on a fixed grid.

Parameters:

component (Component) – An analytic Method I component.

settings (Settings)

q (array, optional) – The grid; inversion_nodes where None.

steps (dict[tuple, dict[str, Any]] | None)

Returns:

q, f (array) – The grid and the rows (the forward’s, unchanged).

jac (dict) – {"beta_c": dF/dbeta_c, "r_a": dF/dR_a}, the parameters the family
has.

record (dict) – How the exponent’s part was taken ("central" or "one-sided"),
its steps, the kernel’s accuracy and its Richardson residual max
|E(d) - E(d/2)| over the column’s scale max |dF/dbeta_c| and,
one-sided, the two sides’ spread over the same scale. The accuracy
is one maximum over the whole column, whose entries can span some
thirty decades (the largest near the center), so the steps suit the
largest entries; an entry far below them is differenced at the same
steps.

Raises:

InputError – Where the component is not analytic, or a Cuddeford Type II, or its
    family has no parameter.

Return type:

tuple[ndarray, ndarray, dict[str, ndarray], dict[str, Any]]

pianistpy.df.gradient.table_jacobian(component, settings, q=None, steps=None)

Return the DF table’s values and their derivatives in the component’s
anisotropy parameters, the forward’s grid and discrete choices held.

Parameters:

component (Component) – An analytic Method I component.

settings (Settings)

q (array, optional) – The grid; inversion_nodes where None.

steps (dict, optional) – The caller’s store of the exponent’s measured steps
(_table_difference): read where it has them, filled where it has
not; without one they are measured at this call.

Returns:

values (dict) – The table as inversion_df makes it, as arrays: k, log_df,
log_df_slope (the rows; zero derivative where a Type II DF is
outside its support), and where the table has them k_below,
log_df_below, log_df_slope_below; the form above the anchor
central (kappa, a_anchor, b, d) and the tail tail (A, a, k).

jac (dict) – {theta: {key: d value / d theta}} for the keys of values but the
energies.

record (dict) – The exponent’s part of the rows ("rows") and of the nodes below
the floor ("below"), as rows_jacobian states it.

Raises:

InputError – As rows_jacobian; and where the form above the anchor is used and
    the center is not on its regular branch (the critical band).

Return type:

tuple[dict[str, ndarray], dict[str, dict[str, ndarray]], dict[str, Any]]

     On this page

# Exceptions

Module pianistpy.exceptions

Exceptions and warnings raised by PIANISTpy.

exception pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyError(message, result=None)

Raised when a result misses the hard accuracy limit, or cannot be
resolved at the settings’ resolution.

Parameters:

message (str) – The check that failed, its error and where.

result (object, optional) – The result that was refused, complete with its validation report,
where the refusal came after it was built, so that it can be inspected
without a second computation (Settings(write_anyway=True) returns
it instead).

Variables:

result (object or None) – The refused result, or None where the refusal came inside a stage.

Return type:

None

exception pianistpy.exceptions.AccuracyWarning

Issued when a result lies between the stated accuracy and the hard limit.

exception pianistpy.exceptions.InputError(*args)

Raised when an input parameter is outside its admissible range.

Parameters:

args (object)

Return type:

None

exception pianistpy.exceptions.PianistpyError(*args)

Base class of every error raised by PIANISTpy.

Variables:

recent (tuple of str) – The most recent messages of the package when the error was raised,
oldest first. They are kept whatever the verbosity, so that a quiet
run that fails can still say what it was doing.

Parameters:

args (object)

Return type:

None

exception pianistpy.exceptions.PianistpyWarning

Base class of every warning issued by PIANISTpy.

exception pianistpy.exceptions.ResultError(*args)

Raised when a result is not what it is taken for.

A file that does not hold the result it is taken for: an unknown format
version, a data digest that does not match the stored arrays, a parent
whose identity differs from the one the file records, a file that does
not read back as written. Or a stage’s output that fails a structural
check the next stage needs: rows that are not finite or not increasing.

Parameters:

args (object)

Return type:

None

exception pianistpy.exceptions.UnphysicalModelError(message, result=None)

Raised when no valid equilibrium exists for the requested model.

Parameters:

message (str) – The condition that failed and the values involved.

result (object, optional) – The distribution function that was computed before the model was
refused, so that it can be inspected without a second computation.

Variables:

result (object or None) – The distribution function attached to the refusal.

Return type:

None

# Functions by subpackage

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/

# Functions by subpackage

Docstrings cite two documents. An equation of Chiang+(2026d) is cited by its own label in that paper,
for example “Chiang+(2026d), Eq. (B9)”. An equation, section or table of the technical notes is cited by its number, which carries the prefix “T:”, together with a fixed key in brackets, for
example “Eq. (T:2.4) [conditions]”, “Section T:2.3.1 [df-form]” or “Table T:2.1 [critical]”; the key is the
item’s label and does not change when the notes are revised and a number moves.

The package

Density profiles

Velocity anisotropy

Particles

Observables

# Inference

# Inference

Module pianistpy.inference

The log-likelihood of a model against data.

class pianistpy.inference.Data(observable, values, r_2d=None, apertures=(), errors=None, covariance=None, unit_system='internal', v_edges=None, r=None)

Measurements of one observable, with their errors.

Parameters:

observable (str) – One of "sigma_los", "sigma_los_aperture", "losvd",
"losvd_aperture", "pdf_v", "h3" and "h4". What was
measured: the line-of-sight dispersion at projected radii, or
averaged over apertures (weighted by the surface density); or a
binned distribution of velocity: the line-of-sight velocity
distribution at one projected radius or in one aperture, or the
local speed distribution at one 3D radius; or a Gauss-Hermite
moment of the line-of-sight velocity distribution at projected radii
or inside apertures (gauss_hermite_moments; dimensionless).

values (array-like, shape (n,)) – The measured values. For a binned distribution, the share of the
distribution inside the window [v_edges[0], v_edges[-1]] that
falls in each bin.

r_2d (array-like, shape (n,), optional) – The projected radii, for "sigma_los" and for moments at radii;
one radius for "losvd".

apertures (sequence of Aperture, optional) – The apertures, for "sigma_los_aperture" and for moments over
apertures, their lengths in the units of the data; one aperture for
"losvd_aperture".

errors (array-like, shape (n,), optional) – The standard deviations of independent errors.

covariance (array-like, shape (n, n), optional) – The covariance of the errors, in place of errors.

unit_system ({"internal", "model", "physical"}) – The units of the data: in the physical system radii in parsecs and
speeds in kilometers per second. A model is compared in the same
system.

v_edges (array-like, shape (n + 1,), optional) – The edges of the bins of a binned distribution, increasing; speeds
of "pdf_v" not negative.

r (array-like, shape (1,), optional) – The 3D radius of "pdf_v".

property identity: str

a digest of everything it holds.

Type:

The identity string of the data

write(path, overwrite=False)

Write the data to a file; pianistpy.read reads it back.

Parameters:

path (str | PathLike)

overwrite (bool)

Return type:

None

class pianistpy.inference.Likelihood(tables, blocks, weights, scale, length, velocity, r_min, r_max, free=(), theta=None, members=(), readings=(), binned=())

The log-likelihood of a model against data, as a JAX function.

Built by likelihood. Called with the weights of the components and the
scales of the units, it returns the Gaussian log-likelihood, traceable
and differentiable in both.

Variables:

tables (tuple) – The projected table of each component, read in JAX.

blocks (tuple) – Each Data, prepared.

weights (array, shape (n_components,)) – The model’s own weights (its components’ masses).

scale (array, shape (2,)) – The model’s own mass and length scales in the data’s units.

velocity (length,) – The factors of the data’s units at the model’s own scales.

r_max (r_min,) – The innermost and outermost projected radius of the tables, in
internal units.

free (tuple of int) – The components whose anisotropy
(\(\beta_{\rm c}\), \(R_{\rm a}\)) is a parameter.

theta (array, shape (n_free, 2)) – Their own (\(\beta_{\rm c}\), \(R_{\rm a}\)), in internal units.

members (tuple) – Their tables at any theta, on the host.

readings (tuple) – Their \(\sigma_{\rm los}^2\) readings as JAX functions of theta.

Parameters:

tables (tuple[_Table, ...])

blocks (tuple[_Block | _Moments | _PointMoments, ...])

weights (Any)

scale (Any)

length (float)

velocity (float)

r_min (float)

r_max (float)

free (tuple[int, ...])

theta (Any | None)

members (tuple[_Free, ...])

readings (tuple[Any, ...])

binned (tuple[_BinnedBlock, ...])

pianistpy.inference.likelihood(model, data, settings=None, free=())

Return the log-likelihood of a model against data, prepared.

The projected table of each component is computed here, once; the
returned function reads them in JAX. A model or data that cannot be
compared are refused here, with an exception.

Parameters:

model (Model) – A model of one component, or a superposition (superpose), in the
unit system of the data.

data (Data or sequence of Data) – The measurements; their log-likelihoods are summed.

settings (Settings, optional) – Numerical settings of the observables; the model’s by default.

free (sequence of int, optional) – The components whose anisotropy
(\(\beta_{\rm c}\), \(R_{\rm a}\)) is a parameter of the
likelihood (its theta): each a spatially finite model on a
truncated profile (a DF inverted on its parent’s profile). An
isotropic or constant member’s \(\beta_{\rm c}\) is free and its
\(R_{\rm a}\) column is held at its own value (infinite), with a
zero gradient: the family has no \(R_{\rm a}\).

Returns:

likelihood

Return type:

Likelihood

Notes

Each measurement is the surface-density weighted mean of
\(\sigma_{\rm los}^2\) over its nodes, sum_j q_ij Sigma(x_j)
sigma^2(x_j) / sum_j q_ij Sigma(x_j): for a projected radius one node,
for an aperture the nodes and weights of aperture_dispersion. On a
superposition each component’s table is its member’s own, on the shared
density, and the two sums are mixed by the weights (mixture): the
measurement is a ratio of two sums linear in the weights. A scale
of length other than the model’s own moves the nodes (x = R / (L l))
and keeps their weights, a change of variable to the data’s radius in
which the aperture is fixed.

A free component’s tables at a theta are built on the host when the
function first meets it: its DF on its truncated profile (refused there,
the function is minus infinity), then the two tables, their rows placed
at that theta. The gradient in theta is that of the reading on those rows
(their placement frozen); between placements the value moves within the
tables’ tolerance. An untruncated component is not free: its edge terms
read its DF.

A Gauss-Hermite moment ("h3", "h4") over an aperture is that of
the mixture’s distribution in the aperture, the components’ own
(aperture_losvd, each on its velocity nodes, mirrored to both signs)
weighted by weight and projected mass, with its own mean and dispersion
as gauss_hermite_moments takes them: traced in the weights; the mass
scale leaves it. Its distributions are read at the model’s own radii, so
the length scale is held there (until a traced reader of each member’s
distribution in radius lands). Moments at projected radii
are read on a model of one component from its moments’ table
(gauss_hermite_table, read_traced) at the radii the length scale
moves, so they are traced in it too. Neither is served with a free
component: its distributions are read at its own theta.

pianistpy.inference.log_likelihood(model, data, settings=None)

Return the Gaussian log-likelihood of a model against data.

Parameters:

model (Model) – The model, in the unit system of the data.

data (Data or sequence of Data) – The measurements; their log-likelihoods are summed.

settings (Settings, optional) – Numerical settings of the observables; the model’s by default.

Returns:

log_likelihood

Return type:

float

Notes

With residuals r of the measured values against the model’s, and
errors e or a covariance C, -r^T C^-1 r / 2 - ln det(2 pi C) / 2.
The value of likelihood at the model’s own weights and scales.

     On this page

Return the SHA-256 digest of every dataset of a file.

The digest covers, for each dataset in the sorted order of its path, the
path, the type, the shape and the raw bytes. Attributes are excluded, so
the digest can be stored in the file it describes.

pianistpy.io.write_table(path, columns, header=(), overwrite=False)

Write named columns as fixed-width text with a header.

The header lines, each starting with #, are written as given,
followed by # columns: and the column names in order. Each row holds
one value of every column, 25 characters a field: a float with 14 digits
after the point in exponent form, an integer as it is. The file is read
back with numpy.loadtxt and compared with the values written, to the
digits written; a file that does not read back is refused.

Parameters:

path (path) – File to write.

columns (mapping of str to array-like) – The columns, in order; one-dimensional, numeric, of one length. A
name holds no space.

header (sequence of str, optional) – Lines for the head of the file, without the leading #.

overwrite (bool, optional) – Replace an existing file.

Raises:

InputError – For a column that is not one-dimensional and numeric, columns of
    different lengths, a name with a space, or an existing file without
    overwrite.

ResultError – If the file does not read back as written.

Return type:

None

# Numerics

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/numerics

# Numerics

Module pianistpy.numerics

Shared numerical leaves: quadrature, interpolation and special functions.

pianistpy.numerics.gauss_legendre(n_nodes)

Return the Gauss-Legendre nodes and weights on [-1, 1].

The nodes of a given count are computed once per session and returned as
read-only arrays, so that no caller can change them for another.

Parameters:

n_nodes (int) – Number of nodes, at least 1.

Returns:

nodes (array, shape (n_nodes,)) – Nodes in increasing order.

weights (array, shape (n_nodes,)) – Weights; they sum to 2.

Return type:

tuple[Any, Any]

Examples

```
>>> nodes, weights = gauss_legendre(2)
>>> float(weights.sum())
2.0

```

pianistpy.numerics.gauss_legendre_unit(n_nodes)

Return the Gauss-Legendre nodes and weights on [0, 1].

Parameters:

n_nodes (int) – Number of nodes, at least 1.

Returns:

nodes (array, shape (n_nodes,)) – Nodes in increasing order.

weights (array, shape (n_nodes,)) – Weights; they sum to 1.

Return type:

tuple[Any, Any]

pianistpy.numerics.hermite(x, x_nodes, f_nodes, df_dx_nodes)

Return the cubic Hermite interpolant and its derivative.

Between two nodes the interpolant is the cubic that takes the values and
the slopes given at both. Outside the nodes it continues as the straight
line through the end node with the end slope.

Parameters:

x (array-like) – Points of evaluation.

x_nodes (array, shape (n,)) – Nodes, strictly increasing.

f_nodes (array, shape (n,)) – Values at the nodes.

df_dx_nodes (array, shape (n,)) – Slopes at the nodes.

Returns:

f (array) – The interpolant at x.

df_dx (array) – Its derivative at x.

Return type:

tuple[Any, Any]

Examples

A cubic is reproduced exactly from its values and slopes at two nodes:

```
>>> import numpy as np
>>> x_nodes = np.array([0.0, 2.0])
>>> f, df_dx = hermite(1.0, x_nodes, x_nodes**3, 3.0 * x_nodes**2)
>>> float(f), float(df_dx)
(1.0, 3.0)

```

pianistpy.numerics.hermite_inverse(f, x_nodes, f_nodes, df_dx_nodes)

Return where an increasing cubic Hermite interpolant takes given values.

The root is bracketed by the two nodes whose values enclose the target,
or by the straight continuation beyond the end nodes, and found by
bisection. Newton steps then refine it; a step that would leave the
bracket is not taken, so a locally steep interpolant cannot throw a root
out of its interval.

Parameters:

f (array-like) – Values to invert for.

x_nodes (array, shape (n,)) – Nodes, strictly increasing.

f_nodes (array, shape (n,)) – Values at the nodes, increasing.

df_dx_nodes (array, shape (n,)) – Slopes at the nodes, positive at the two end nodes.

Returns:

x (array) – Points at which the interpolant equals f.

residual (float) – Largest absolute difference between the interpolant at x and f.

Return type:

tuple[Any, float]

Examples

```
>>> import numpy as np
>>> x_nodes = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0])
>>> x, residual = hermite_inverse(1.5, x_nodes, 2.0 * x_nodes, np.full(3, 2.0))
>>> float(x), residual
(0.75, 0.0)

```

     On this page

# Observables

Module pianistpy.observables

Observables: dispersions, line-of-sight velocity distributions and apertures.

class pianistpy.observables.Aperture(shape, r_off=0.0, r_ape=None, side_x=None, side_y=None, angle=0.0)

An aperture on the plane of the sky, circular or rectangular.

Build one with Aperture.circle or Aperture.rectangle. Lengths are
in the unit system of the model (or table) it is used with, as the
observables’ radii are.

Parameters:

shape ({"circle", "rectangle"}) – Shape of the aperture.

r_off (float) – Projected distance \(R_{\rm off}\) of the center of the aperture
from the center of the model.

r_ape (float, optional) – Radius \(R_{\rm ape}\) of a circle.

side_x (float, optional) – Full sides of a rectangle.

side_y (float, optional) – Full sides of a rectangle.

angle (float, optional) – For a rectangle, the angle between its x side and the direction from
its center to the center of the model, in radians.

Examples

```
>>> Aperture.circle(1.0, r_off=10.0).shape
'circle'
>>> Aperture.rectangle(2.0, 0.5, r_off=10.0, angle=0.3).side_y
0.5

```

classmethod circle(r_ape, r_off=0.0)

Return a circular aperture of radius r_ape at offset r_off.

Parameters:

r_ape (float)

r_off (float)

Return type:

Aperture

classmethod rectangle(side_x, side_y, r_off=0.0, angle=0.0)

Return a rectangular aperture of full sides side_x by side_y.

Its center is at offset r_off, and angle is the angle between its
x side and the direction from its center to the center of the model.

Parameters:

side_x (float)

side_y (float)

r_off (float)

angle (float)

Return type:

Aperture

arc(r)

Return the angular measure of the circle of radius r inside the
aperture, in radians.

For a circle it is the closed form of the overlap of two circles:
\(2\pi\) where the whole circle is inside, zero where it is
outside, and the band
\(4 \arcsin\sqrt{x/2}\) with
\(x = [R_{\rm ape}^2 - (r - R_{\rm off})^2] / (2 r R_{\rm off})\)
between. For a rectangle, each of the four edges is a half-plane
constraint on the angle that becomes active at angles in closed form;
those angles cut the circle into intervals on which membership is
constant, and the measure is the length of the intervals whose
midpoint lies inside. One code path serves a rectangle that contains
the center of the model, touches it, or is clear of it.

Parameters:

r (array-like) – Projected radii, not negative.

Returns:

arc

Return type:

array, the shape of r

breaks()

Return the radii at which arc is not smooth, increasing.

For a circle: the edges of the band and, where the aperture contains
the center of the model, the radius at which the full circle ends.
For a rectangle: the perpendicular distances from the center of the
model to the four edge lines, kept where the foot of the perpendicular
lies on the edge, and the distances to the four corners; at most
eight radii, between two of which arc is smooth.

Return type:

list[float]

to_dict()

Return the aperture as a plain dictionary.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

classmethod from_dict(record)

Build the aperture from its dictionary form.

Parameters:

record (Mapping[str, Any])

Return type:

Aperture

class pianistpy.observables.Differentiable(model, settings=None)

A model’s observables as JAX functions of its anisotropy.

Built once from a model of one component on a truncated profile (a DF
inverted on its parent’s profile, as truncate makes it): its tables are
computed here, at the model’s own anisotropy. Each method takes
theta = (beta_c, R_a), the component’s anisotropy in internal units,
first, and is a JAX function of it, traceable and differentiable.

Parameters:

model (Model) – A model of one component on a truncated profile, spatially finite,
whose family has \(\beta_{\rm c}\) or \(R_{\rm a}\): constant
anisotropy (\(\beta_{\rm c}\); an isotropic or constant
component’s \(R_{\rm a}\) is held at its own, infinite, value with
a zero gradient), Cuddeford Type I (both), Osipkov-Merritt Type I and
Type II (\(R_{\rm a}\)).

settings (Settings, optional) – Numerical settings of the observables; the model’s by default.

Variables:

model (Model) – The model.

theta (array, shape (2,)) – Its own \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\), in internal units.

Raises:

InputError – For a superposition or a model of several components, a component not
    spatially finite or not on a truncated profile that carries its
    parent’s DF, and a family whose observables are not differentiable
    (Cuddeford Type II), each named.

Notes

Radii and velocities are in internal units, whatever the model’s unit
system: theta, as the likelihood’s, is internal, and so is everything a
method reads and returns.

A method’s value at a theta is computed on the host the first time the
method meets it: the DF inverted at theta on the component’s truncated
profile, then the observable’s tables, at the cost of the likelihood’s
own rebuild of a free component (about that of the plain call on the
model rebuilt at theta); the last eight theta are kept. At a theta where
the model is refused the value is NaN and its gradient zero. The
derivative is the observable’s tangent rows in theta on the tables’ own
rows, their placement frozen: between two placements the value moves by
the tables’ tolerance, which the derivative does not carry. A method is
not differentiable in its radii (their gradient is NaN).

sigma_r(theta, r)

Return the radial velocity dispersion at radii, as
pianistpy.sigma_r of the model at theta.

Parameters:

theta (array-like, shape (2,)) – The component’s \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\), in internal units.

r (array-like) – Radii, in internal units.

Returns:

sigma_r – The dispersion in internal units, with the shape of r; NaN where
the model at theta is refused.

Return type:

array

sigma_t(theta, r)

Return the tangential velocity dispersion at radii (both tangential
components together), as pianistpy.sigma_t of the model at theta.

Parameters:

theta (array-like, shape (2,)) – The component’s \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\), in internal units.

r (array-like) – Radii, in internal units.

Returns:

sigma_t – The dispersion in internal units, with the shape of r; NaN where
the model at theta is refused.

Return type:

array

sigma_los(theta, r_2d)

Return the line-of-sight velocity dispersion at projected radii, as
pianistpy.sigma_los of the model at theta.

Parameters:

theta (array-like, shape (2,)) – The component’s \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\), in internal units.

r_2d (array-like) – Projected radii, in internal units.

Returns:

sigma_los – The dispersion in internal units, with the shape of r_2d; zero
beyond the last row, NaN where the model at theta is refused.

Return type:

array

sigma_los_aperture(theta, aperture)

Return the line-of-sight velocity dispersion averaged over an
aperture, weighted by the surface density, as
pianistpy.sigma_los_aperture of the model at theta.

Parameters:

theta (array-like, shape (2,)) – The component’s \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\), in internal units.

aperture (Aperture) – The aperture, its lengths in internal units.

Returns:

sigma_los – The dispersion in internal units; NaN where the model at theta is
refused.

Return type:

scalar array

Notes

The derivative is the aperture’s integral of the tangent rows of
\(\sigma_{\rm los}^2\), on the nodes and weights of the plain call’s own
quadrature (the integral is linear in the rows), over twice the value.

losvd(theta, r_2d, v)

Return the line-of-sight velocity distribution at the pairs
(r_2d, v), as pianistpy.losvd of the model at theta.

Parameters:

theta (array-like, shape (2,)) – The component’s \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\), in internal units.

r_2d (array-like) – Projected radii and line-of-sight velocities, in internal units;
they broadcast against each other.

v (array-like) – Projected radii and line-of-sight velocities, in internal units;
they broadcast against each other.

Returns:

losvd – The distribution per unit internal velocity, with the broadcast
shape; NaN where the model at theta is refused.

Return type:

array

Notes

The derivative is the DF path’s, its placement frozen: the reading’s
transpose onto the table’s rows (losvd_read_vjp), the rows’ onto the
DF’s table and forms (losvd_rows_vjp) with the rows’ explicit part
in the anisotropy, and the DF table’s derivative in theta
(df.gradient.table_jacobian). Not differentiable in r_2d or v.

pdf_v(theta, r, v)

Return the local speed distribution at the pairs (r, v), as
pianistpy.pdf_v of the model at theta.

Parameters:

theta (array-like, shape (2,)) – The component’s \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\), in internal units.

r (array-like) – Radii and speeds, in internal units; they broadcast against each
other.

v (array-like) – Radii and speeds, in internal units; they broadcast against each
other.

Returns:

pdf_v – The distribution per unit internal velocity, with the broadcast
shape; NaN where the model at theta is refused.

Return type:

array

Notes

The derivative is the DF path’s: at each radius the speed
distribution’s transpose (speed_distribution_vjp) at the speeds
asked, the distribution there computed by the rule its record
certified, as SpeedDistribution.read computes it, with its explicit
part in the anisotropy, and the DF table’s derivative in theta. Not
differentiable in r or v.

aperture_losvd(theta, aperture, v)

Return the line-of-sight velocity distribution inside an aperture
at the velocities v, as pianistpy.aperture_losvd of the model at
theta.

Parameters:

theta (array-like, shape (2,)) – The component’s \((\beta_{\rm c}, R_{\rm a})\), in internal units.

aperture (Aperture) – The aperture, its lengths in internal units.

v (array-like) – Line-of-sight velocities, in internal units.

Returns:

losvd – The distribution per unit internal velocity, with the shape of
v; NaN where the model at theta is refused.

Return type:

array

Notes

The derivative is the DF path’s: the transpose of the reading of the
aperture’s panels (each panel’s polynomial through its nodes) onto
its values at the nodes, theirs onto the table’s rows
(aperture_losvd_vjp), then as losvd. Not differentiable in v.

class pianistpy.observables.LosTable(model)

The line-of-sight velocity distributions of a model, built once.

The object holds the table of line-of-sight velocity distributions over
projected radius that the aperture quantities read. It is built when the
object is created and reused by every observable computed from it.

Parameters:

model (Model) – The model to project: of one component, or a superposition
(superpose).

Variables:

model (Model) – The model, whose unit system the observables read from this object
are given in.

table (profile, projected, kept,) – The results of the stages dispersion_profile,
projected_dispersion, kept_ranges and losvd_table, at the
model’s settings; of the first component for a superposition.

validation (ValidationReport) – The checks of the table (those of validate_table) and the worst
tier of the model; for a superposition, each check at its worst over
the components. A table above the goal says so in a warning.

parts (tuple of LosTable) – One table per component of a superposition, each of the component
as a model of one component; (self,) for a model of one
component.

to(system, **kwargs)

Return the same tables presented in another unit system.

Nothing is recomputed: the tables stay in internal units, and the
observables read from the returned object are given in the units of
self.model.to(system, **kwargs) (Model.to).

Parameters:

system (str)

kwargs (Any)

Return type:

LosTable

close()

Close the worker processes the table’s aperture calls keep.

The first aperture read from a table that needs workers starts a pool
of them, and the table’s later apertures reuse it; the pool closes
here, or when the table is gone. A table presented in another unit
system (to) shares the pool. An aperture read after close starts
a new one.

Return type:

None

class pianistpy.observables.ProjectedSampler(source, R_range, v_range=None)

Draw pairs of projected radius and line-of-sight velocity.

Pairs follow \(p(R, v) \propto 2\pi R\,\Sigma(R)\,D(v\,|\,R)\) on
the annulus R_range and in the window v_range, exactly conditioned:
the radius’s distribution carries the window’s share at each radius.
Exact for every anisotropy (the distribution is the line of sight’s
marginal, the angles integrated in the table).

Parameters:

source (Model or LosTable) – The model (its LosTable is built first) or its prepared table; of
one component or a superposition.

R_range ((float, float)) – The annulus, in the source’s unit system (Model.to): internal units
by default, parsecs (floats or Astropy quantities) in the physical
system. An end beyond the table’s rows is taken at the row where the
surface density beyond it is within INNER_DISK_TOLERANCE of the
annulus’s, and refused otherwise.

v_range ((float, float), optional) – The window of line-of-sight velocity, signed, in the source’s unit
system (km/s in the physical system); the whole distribution where
None.

Variables:

validation (ValidationReport) – v_table: the reading’s error in the cumulative, between grid
radii and between nodes; window: the window ends’ reading;
radius_quadrature: the mass integral against a finer rule,
relative; row_norm: the rows’ distance from unit integral;
annulus_cut: the share cut at the table’s ends.

mass (float) – The annulus’s mass in the window, internal units.

Raises:

InputError – Where the annulus lies outside the table, overlaps an interval the
    table left uncertified, or the window holds none of the
    distribution.

sample(n, seed=0)

Draw n pairs.

Pair i draws from its own key as Sampler does: the radius from the
channel radius, the velocity from speed and, of a
superposition, the component (by its share of the annulus’s mass in
the window) from component; so a draw is the same pair by pair
for any n.

Returns:

pairs

Return type:

ProjectedPairs

Parameters:

n (int)

seed (int)

pianistpy.observables.aperture_losvd(source, aperture, v)

Return the line-of-sight velocity distribution inside an aperture.

Parameters:

source (Model or LosTable) – The model, or its prepared LosTable. Given a model, its table is
built first (LosTable), at every call: where a model is read more
than once, build its table once with pp.LosTable(model) and pass
the table.

aperture (Aperture) – The aperture, built with Aperture.circle or Aperture.rectangle,
its lengths in the model’s unit system (parsecs in the physical
system).

v (array-like) – Line-of-sight velocity in the model’s unit system (km/s, a float or
an Astropy quantity, in the physical system).

Returns:

losvd – The probability density of the line-of-sight velocity of the
tracers inside the aperture, weighted by the surface density over
it, at each v, per unit velocity of the model’s unit system (an
Astropy quantity in the physical system), with the shape of v. It
is even in \(v\), integrates to one over all \(v\), and is
zero beyond the escape velocity along the line of sight.

Return type:

array

Notes

The distribution is the stage aperture_losvd, on Gauss-Legendre
panels in velocity refined until its norm and second moment agree with
the table’s rows; at any v it is read by each panel’s polynomial
through its own nodes, the polynomial its quadrature integrates. Its
second moment is sigma_los_aperture’s from the same LosTable, and
it is checked against the aperture’s dispersion (validate_aperture):
a distribution above the goal, or read from a table above it, says so
in a warning.

Of a superposition, each component’s distribution inside the aperture
is summed with its weight times its projected mass inside the
aperture: \(D = \sum_k w_k M_k D_k / \sum_k w_k M_k\).

pianistpy.observables.losvd(source, r_2d, v)

Return the line-of-sight velocity distribution at projected radii.

Parameters:

source (Model or LosTable) – The model, or its prepared LosTable. Given a model, its table is
built first (LosTable), at every call: where a model is read more
than once, build its table once with pp.LosTable(model) and pass
the table.

r_2d (array-like) – Projected radius \(R_{\rm 2D}\) in the model’s unit system
(Model.to): internal units by default, parsecs (a float or an
Astropy quantity) in the physical system.

v (array-like) – Line-of-sight velocity in the model’s unit system (km/s, a float or
an Astropy quantity, in the physical system). r_2d and v
broadcast against each other.

Returns:

losvd – The probability density of the line-of-sight velocity at each pair
\((R_{\rm 2D}, v)\), per unit velocity of the model’s unit
system (an Astropy quantity in the physical system), with the
broadcast shape of r_2d and v. It is even in \(v\), integrates
to one over all \(v\), and is zero beyond the escape velocity
along the line of sight.

Return type:

array

Notes

Between the rows of the table the distribution is read through the
table’s own stencil, the reading the table certified its rows for; a
projected radius inside an uncertified interval is refused by name.

Of a superposition, each component’s distribution is read from its own
table and the components are summed with their weights times their
surface densities: \(D = \sum_k w_k \Sigma_k D_k / \sum_k w_k
\Sigma_k\).

pianistpy.observables.pdf_v(source, r, v)

Return the local speed distribution at 3D radii.

Parameters:

source (Model or LosTable) – The model, or its prepared LosTable (whose intrinsic second
moments the distribution is checked against).

r (array-like) – Radius \(r\) in the model’s unit system (Model.to): internal
units by default, parsecs (a float or an Astropy quantity) in the
physical system.

v (array-like) – Speed in the model’s unit system (km/s, a float or an Astropy
quantity, in the physical system). r and v broadcast against
each other.

Returns:

pdf_v – The probability density of the speed \(V = |\mathbf{v}|\) at
each pair \((r, V)\), per unit velocity of the model’s unit
system (an Astropy quantity in the physical system), with the
broadcast shape of r and v. It integrates to one over
\(V \geq 0\) and is zero beyond the end of the DF’s support,
the escape speed but for a Type II model, whose speeds reach
\(V_{\rm esc}/\sqrt{1 - r^2/r_a^2}\) (its unbound share is
SpeedDistribution.unbound_fraction).

Return type:

array

Raises:

AccuracyError – Where the distribution at a radius is beyond the hard limit, unless
    the model’s settings ask for it anyway (write_anyway).

Notes

Each radius is the stage speed_distribution, certified by its norm
against the density, its second moment against the Jeans dispersion
and the change of its angle rule; the distribution at the speeds asked
is read by the rule it certified. Of a superposition, the components are
mixed by their density at the radius: \(p = \sum_k w_k \varrho_k
p_k / \sum_k w_k \varrho_k\).

References

Chiang+(2026d), Sect. 5.1 and [eqn:rho_f_anisotropic_scale].

pianistpy.observables.sigma_los_aperture(source, aperture)

Return the velocity dispersion inside an aperture.

Given a model, only the projected radii the aperture covers are computed.

Parameters:

source (Model or LosTable) – The model, or its prepared LosTable.

aperture (Aperture) – The aperture, built with Aperture.circle or Aperture.rectangle,
its lengths in the model’s unit system (parsecs in the physical
system).

Returns:

sigma_ape – Velocity dispersion inside the aperture, in the model’s unit system.

Return type:

float

Notes

Given a model, the second moment of the line-of-sight dispersion averaged
over the aperture with the surface density (aperture_dispersion), which
reads no velocity distribution. Given a LosTable, the second moment of
the aperture’s velocity distribution (aperture_losvd) by its own
weights. The two agree to the accuracy goal (validate_aperture); a
distribution above the goal, or read from a table above it, says so in a
warning.

Of a superposition, the components are summed with their weights under
the aperture: given a model, the surface-density weighted sums of
\(\sigma_{\rm los}^2\) and of the surface density, each component’s
own, on the aperture’s nodes of the first component (the components
share one density), mixed as for sigma_los; given a LosTable, the
second moment of the aperture distributions summed with the weights
times each component’s projected mass inside the aperture, each
distribution checked against its own component’s aperture dispersion.

pianistpy.observables.sigma_los(source, r_2d)

Return the line-of-sight velocity dispersion at projected radii.

Parameters:

source (Model or LosTable) – The model, or its prepared LosTable.

r_2d (array-like) – Projected radius \(R_{\rm 2D}\) in the model’s unit system
(Model.to): internal units by default, parsecs (a float or an
Astropy quantity) in the physical system.

Returns:

sigma_los – Line-of-sight velocity dispersion in the model’s unit system, with
the shape of r_2d.

Return type:

array

Notes

Of a superposition, \(\sigma_{\rm los}^2 = \sum_k w_k \Sigma_k
\sigma_{{\rm los},k}^2 / \sum_k w_k \Sigma_k\), each component read from
its own table; zero beyond the last row.

pianistpy.observables.sigma_r(source, r)

Return the radial velocity dispersion at radii.

Parameters:

source (Model or LosTable) – The model, or its prepared LosTable, whose intrinsic second
moments are read.

r (array-like) – Radius \(r\) in the model’s unit system (Model.to): internal
units by default, parsecs (a float or an Astropy quantity) in the
physical system.

Returns:

sigma_r – Radial velocity dispersion \(\sigma_r\) in the model’s unit
system, with the shape of r.

Return type:

array

Notes

The reading between the grid points of the intrinsic profile is that of
DispersionProfile.read. Of a superposition, whose components share one
density, \(\sigma_r^2 = \sum_k w_k \sigma_{r,k}^2\).

pianistpy.observables.sigma_t(source, r)

Return the tangential velocity dispersion at radii.

Parameters:

source (Model or LosTable) – The model, or its prepared LosTable.

r (array-like) – Radius \(r\) in the model’s unit system, as for sigma_r.

Returns:

sigma_t – Tangential velocity dispersion of both tangential components
together, \(\sigma_{\rm t}^2 = \sigma_\theta^2 + \sigma_\phi^2\)
\(= 2 (1 - \beta_\sigma) \sigma_r^2\), in the model’s unit system,
with the shape of r.

Return type:

array

Notes

Read as sigma_r is; of a superposition, \(\sigma_{\rm t}^2 =
\sum_k w_k \sigma_{{\rm t},k}^2\).

## The speed distribution’s stage

Module pianistpy.observables.stages

The stage behind pianistpy.observables.pdf_v(), at one radius, with its record (Local speed distribution).

pianistpy.observables.stages.speed_distribution(model, r, settings, profile=None)

Return the local speed distribution of a model at a 3D radius.

Parameters:

model (Model) – A model of one component.

r (float) – Radius, in internal units, inside the profile and, for Type II,
inside the anisotropy radius.

settings (Settings) – Numerical settings (the observables group’s
n_speed_angle_nodes, n_speed_angle_panels and
speed_tolerance).

profile (DispersionProfile, optional) – The model’s intrinsic second moments, which the second moment is
checked against; computed when not given.

Returns:

distribution

Return type:

SpeedDistribution

Raises:

InputError – For a model of more than one component, or a radius outside the
    profile or, for Type II, at or beyond the anisotropy radius.

Notes

\(p(V\,|\,r) = (4\pi/\varrho)\, r^{-2b} V^{2-2b} \int_0^1
(1-t^2)^{-b} f(Q)\,{\rm d}t\) over the DF’s own support (_speed), with
\(t = \cos\eta\), the angle between the velocity and the radius,
the variable of the sampler’s angle law. The DF module states the
support (AsymptoticForm.below_floor): F is read through its lookup,
zero below its first energy where its rule is "zero". A Type II DF
is a function of \(Q_+ = Z + L^2/(2r_a^2)\), so its speeds reach
\(V_{\rm max} = \sqrt{2(\mathcal{P} - K_c)/(1 - r^2/r_a^2)}\),
beyond the escape speed where its floor \(K_c\) is below
\(\xi\mathcal{P}(r)\), \(\xi = r^2/r_a^2\), and
unbound_fraction is the share there. A Type II model is truncated at
\(K_t \geq \mathcal{P}(r_a)\) (truncate’s domain gate), so its
floor in the truncated potential is zero and its unbound share is not.
A floor at \(\mathcal{P}(r_a)\) itself, in the potential that
vanishes at infinity, would leave no orbit unbound:
\(Z \geq (\mathcal{P}(r_a) - \xi\mathcal{P}(r))/(1 - \xi) > 0\), since
\(r^2\mathcal{P}(r)\) increases with \(r\) (its derivative
\(2r\mathcal{P} - M(r) \geq M(r) > 0\), as
\(\mathcal{P} \geq M(r)/r\) there).

The angle rule’s nodes double, at most SPEED_DOUBLINGS times, until
the distribution on the speed rule changes by less than
speed_tolerance of its largest value. On an untruncated Type I DF
that diverges at its floor (a tail \(F \propto K^{-1/2}\) with a
logarithmic factor) the distribution is infinite at exactly
\(V_*\), an integrable singularity; speeds within
SPEED_KINK_GAP of it are left out of that check.

References

Chiang+(2026d) [eqn:rho_f_anisotropic_scale], [eqn:varphi_prob], [eqn:V_prob].

     On this page

# Particles

Module pianistpy.particles

Particle sampling: the prepared sampler and the particle result.

class pianistpy.particles.Particles(position, velocity, mass, component, component_names, unit_system, units, identity, parent)

A particle realization of a model.

Parameters:

position (array, shape (n, 3)) – Cartesian positions.

velocity (array, shape (n, 3)) – Cartesian velocities.

mass (array, shape (n,)) – Particle masses.

component (array of int, shape (n,)) – Index, into component_names, of the component each particle
belongs to.

component_names (tuple of str) – Names of the components of the model.

unit_system ({"internal", "model", "physical"}) – The unit system of the arrays. Internal by default everywhere.

units (dict of str to str) – Unit of the position, the velocity and the mass, as text.

identity (str) – Identity string of the realization.

parent (str) – Identity string of the sampler or model the particles were drawn from.

Notes

The arrays are read-only. Two realizations are compared by their
identity strings.

write(path, layout='native', **options)

Write the particles to a file; see write_particles.

Parameters:

path (str | PathLike)

layout (str)

options (Any)

Return type:

None

class pianistpy.particles.Sampler(model, r_sample=None, r_range=None)

Everything needed to draw particles from a model, built once.

The sampler holds the tables that sampling needs. They are built when the
sampler is created and reused by every call of sample, so a user keeps
one object however many tables there are.

Parameters:

model (Model) – The model to draw from.

r_sample (float, optional) – Outer radius of the sampling, in internal units: the radius table
depends on it. Required for a model that is not spatially finite;
the truncation radius of one that is.

r_range (tuple of float, optional) – Radii (r_lo, r_hi), in internal units, between which every particle
is drawn: 0 <= r_lo < r_hi, r_hi at most the outer radius of the
sampling. The draw is the model’s own conditioned on the range, not a
selection: each particle’s radius number is taken in the mass fractions
of the range (stages.radius_bounds), and the particles carry the
range’s mass. Its other numbers are those of the draw without the range.

Variables:

validation (ValidationReport) – The checks of the tables (those of SpeedTable.validation) and the
worst tier of the model. A sampler above the goal says so in a
warning; one beyond the hard limit is refused.

Raises:

InputError – If model is not a Model, or has more components than this release
    samples, or r_range is not a range of radii inside the sampling.

AccuracyError – If the model’s report reads "refused" and its settings do not ask
    for results from it anyway (Settings, write_anyway), or if a
    speed table lies beyond the hard limit and the settings do not ask for
    it anyway.

Notes

A physical model is not thereby samplable at every tier. The speed
table’s rows are refined until the error across them is under the goal
or their count reaches n_rows_max; close to the smallest anisotropy
radius at which an Osipkov-Merritt or Cuddeford Type I DF is non-negative,
the rows reach n_rows_max first and the error grows steeply as
\(R_{\rm a}\) falls toward that radius. Measured on a truncated NFW
density of concentration 10 at the default tier, the error crosses the hard
limit at 1.02 to 1.2 times that radius and the ceiling at 1.09 to 1.84
times it (up to \(\beta_{\rm c} = 0.4\)), the widest for the most
negative \(\beta_{\rm c}\); at \(\beta_{\rm c} = 1/2\), whose DF is
non-negative at every \(R_{\rm a}\), the table is beyond the hard limit
at every \(R_{\rm a}\) up to 0.32. A constant-anisotropy model is within
the ceiling up to \(\beta_{\rm c} = 0.4\). The bound is measured, not
imposed: the report of each table is the verdict (the user guide,
Particles, gives the table per family).

sample(n, seed=0)

Draw particles from the model.

Parameters:

n (int) – Number of particles.

seed (int, optional) – Seed of the random streams.

Returns:

particles – The particles, in the model’s units (Model.units). Every draw is
made in internal units and converted at the output only.

Return type:

Particles

Raises:

InputError – If n is not a positive integer below 2^31.

AccuracyError – If a particle lies beyond the phase-space bound of its component.

speeds(r, seed=0, v_range=None)

Draw one speed at each given radius, within a window of speeds.

Parameters:

r (array-like, shape (n,)) – Radii, in internal units, inside the sampling: positive and at most
its outer radius.

seed (int, optional) – Seed of the random streams. The speed at the i-th radius takes the
speed number of particle i of sample at the same seed, mapped into
the window’s numbers (and, for a superposition, its component by
the window’s share of each component).

v_range (tuple of float or of array-like, optional) – The speeds (v_lo, v_hi), in internal units, 0 <= v_lo < v_hi. Each
bound is a float, the same window at every radius, or an array that
broadcasts against r, a window at each radius (as a grid in units
of each radius’s escape speed needs). Without it, the whole speed
distribution.

Returns:

v (array, shape (n,)) – The speed at each radius, drawn from the model’s speed distribution
at that radius conditioned on the window, in internal units; NaN at
a radius where the window holds none of the distribution.

fraction (array, shape (n,)) – The fraction of the speed distribution at each radius in the window
(the weighted sum of the components’ fractions for a
superposition).

Raises:

InputError – For a model with a finite anisotropy radius (Osipkov-Merritt or
    Cuddeford): there the speed is the scaled speed times a factor of
    the drawn angle, so the window couples to the angle, and no table
    holds the speed’s distribution at a radius with the angle
    integrated out. Also for radii outside the sampling, an invalid
    window, or bounds that do not broadcast against r.

Return type:

tuple[Any, Any]

pianistpy.particles.component_view(model, k)

Return component k of a superposed model as a model of one component.

Parameters:

model (Model) – A superposed model (is_superposition).

k (int) – Index of the component.

Returns:

view – The component on its own: its table on its own grid, its forms, the
shared truncated profile, and mass 1. The sampler and the observables
read each component of a superposition through it.

Return type:

Model

pianistpy.particles.is_superposition(model)

Return whether a model is a superposition (superpose).

Parameters:

model (Model) – The model.

Returns:

superposed – Whether every component is built on one truncated profile, as
superpose builds them.

Return type:

bool
