# Density profiles

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/profiles

# Density profiles

Module pianistpy.profiles

Density profiles.

class pianistpy.profiles.DoublePowerLaw(rho_alpha, rho_beta, rho_gamma)

Double-power-law density profile in internal units.

Parameters:

rho_alpha (float) – Sharpness \(\alpha\) of the transition between the inner and the
outer slope. At least 1/2.

rho_beta (float) – Outer logarithmic slope \(\beta\). Greater than 2.

rho_gamma (float) – Inner logarithmic slope \(\gamma\), with
\(0 \leq \gamma < 2\).

Notes

In internal units the scale radius is 1, the central potential is 1 and the
potential vanishes at infinity:

\[\varrho(R) = C\,R^{-\gamma}\,(1 + R^{\alpha})^{(\gamma-\beta)/\alpha} .\]

The lower bound on \(\gamma\) excludes a density that decreases
toward the center; the upper bound keeps the central potential finite.
The bound on \(\beta\) keeps the potential finite at large radii.

The named profiles are parameter sets of this one profile, built by the
class methods nfw, hernquist and plummer. They are not separate
implementations. Where a profile has a closed form for its mass or its
potential, that form is used inside mass and p; the tests hold it to
the general incomplete-Beta form.

References

Chiang+(2026d), Appendix A (labels eqn:double_power_law_MT,
eqn:double_power_law_mass, app:P_beta).

Examples

```
>>> DoublePowerLaw.nfw()
DoublePowerLaw(rho_alpha=1.0, rho_beta=3.0, rho_gamma=1.0)
>>> DoublePowerLaw.hernquist().mass_total
1.0
>>> float(DoublePowerLaw.plummer().p(0.0))
1.0

```

classmethod nfw()

Return the Navarro-Frenk-White profile, (1, 3, 1).

Return type:

DoublePowerLaw

classmethod hernquist()

Return the Hernquist profile, (1, 4, 1).

Return type:

DoublePowerLaw

classmethod plummer()

Return the Plummer profile, (2, 5, 0).

Return type:

DoublePowerLaw

property name: str

Name of the profile, or its parameters if it has none.

property rho_norm: float

Normalization \(C\) of the density, for a central potential of 1.

Notes

\[C = \frac{\alpha\,\Gamma[(\beta-\gamma)/\alpha]}
         {\Gamma[(\beta-2)/\alpha]\,\Gamma[(2-\gamma)/\alpha]} .\]

property mass_total: float

Total mass in internal units; infinite for an outer slope of 3 or less.

rho(r)

Return the density \(\varrho(R)\).

Parameters:

r (array-like) – Radius in internal units.

Returns:

rho – Density in internal units, with the shape of r.

Return type:

array

mass(r)

Return the enclosed mass \(\mathcal{M}(R)\).

Parameters:

r (array-like) – Radius in internal units.

Returns:

mass – Enclosed mass in internal units, with the shape of r.

Return type:

array

Notes

With \(z = R^\alpha/(1+R^\alpha)\),

\[\mathcal{M}(R) = \frac{C}{\alpha}\,
    B\!\left(z;\,\frac{3-\gamma}{\alpha},\,\frac{\beta-3}{\alpha}\right) .\]

p(r)

Return the relative potential \(P(R)\).

Parameters:

r (array-like) – Radius in internal units.

Returns:

p – Relative potential in internal units, with the shape of r. It is 1
at the center and vanishes at infinity.

Return type:

array

Notes

With \(z = R^\alpha/(1+R^\alpha)\), \(a_2 = (2-\gamma)/\alpha\)
and \(b_2 = (\beta-2)/\alpha\),

\[P(R) = \frac{\mathcal{M}(R)}{R}
     + \frac{C}{\alpha}\left[B(a_2, b_2) - B(z;\,a_2, b_2)\right] .\]

depth_inner(r, terms=4)

Return the depth \(u = P(0) - P(R)\) near the center, with no
subtraction, and the series’ own truncation estimate.

Parameters:

r (array-like) – Radius in internal units.

terms (int, optional) – Number of terms of the series.

Returns:

u (array) – The depth from the first terms terms.

bound (array) – The magnitude of the next term relative to u, per point;
infinite where u is not positive.

Return type:

tuple[Any, Any]

Notes

A density term \(C\binom{e}{k}R^{-\gamma+k\alpha}\),
\(e = (\gamma-\beta)/\alpha\), contributes
\(C\binom{e}{k}R^{2-\gamma+k\alpha}/[(2-\gamma+k\alpha)(3-\gamma+k\alpha)]\)
to the depth, term by term.

to_dict()

Return the profile as a plain dictionary.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

classmethod from_dict(record)

Build the profile from its dictionary form.

Parameters:

record (Mapping[str, Any])

Return type:

DoublePowerLaw

class pianistpy.profiles.ProfileTables(log_r, log_p, log_p_slope, log_r_all, log_mass, log_mass_slope, log_rho_coefficients, has_edge_row, r_last, p_last, rho_last, r_t, mass_t, edge_exponent)

The arrays a kernel reads a TruncatedProfile from.

They are the numbers TruncatedProfile.potential, density, mass and
radius evaluate, laid out for a kernel that takes them as traced
arguments: the cubic Hermite in the logarithms on the interior rows and
the edge’s closed forms beyond them.

Parameters:

log_r (array, shape (n_interior,)) – ln r, ln P and d ln P / d ln r at the interior rows (every row but
an edge row).

log_p (array, shape (n_interior,)) – ln r, ln P and d ln P / d ln r at the interior rows (every row but
an edge row).

log_p_slope (array, shape (n_interior,)) – ln r, ln P and d ln P / d ln r at the interior rows (every row but
an edge row).

log_r_all (array, shape (n,)) – ln r, ln M and d ln M / d ln r at every row.

log_mass (array, shape (n,)) – ln r, ln M and d ln M / d ln r at every row.

log_mass_slope (array, shape (n,)) – ln r, ln M and d ln M / d ln r at every row.

log_rho_coefficients (array, shape (n_components, 4, n_interior - 1)) – The coefficients of the cubic spline of ln rho in ln r on each
interval, highest power first, in the interval’s own ln r offset.

has_edge_row (bool) – Whether the profile carries its edge as its last row; the fields
below are read only then.

r_last (float) – Radius and potential of the last interior row.

p_last (float) – Radius and potential of the last interior row.

rho_last (array, shape (n_components,)) – Density of each component there.

r_t (float) – Truncation radius and total mass.

mass_t (float) – Truncation radius and total mass.

edge_exponent (array, shape (n_components,)) – Exponent q of each component’s density at the edge.

class pianistpy.profiles.TruncatedProfile(r, p_trunc, rho_trunc, mass_trunc, k_t, r_t, mass_t, spatially_finite, source, source_anisotropy, model, edge_exponent, u_trunc=<factory>, central_deficit=(), override_r=nan, override_r_end=nan, override_rows=0, override_rule='none', origin=<factory>, df_k=<factory>, df_log_f=<factory>, df_slope=<factory>, df_taylor=(), model_level=None)

The self-consistent profile of a truncated model.

It is the profile of a model, and it can be the profile of a component
of another model: a component given the truncated profile of a parent
model and a new anisotropy is Method II of Chiang+(2026d).

Two profiles are equal where they belong to the same model: the identity
of a model determines its profile.

The profile evaluates itself: potential, density, mass and
radius are the one reading of the rows that every stage of the
package takes, in place of an interpolant of its own. Between the rows
the potential and the mass are cubic Hermite interpolants in the
logarithms with the exact slopes the rows state (the Poisson equation
gives \(\mathrm{d}\ln\mathcal{P}/\mathrm{d}\ln r = -M/(r\mathcal{P})\)
and \(\mathrm{d}\ln M/\mathrm{d}\ln r = r^3\rho/M\)); the density
of each component is a cubic spline in the logarithms, since the rows
state no density slope. On the last interval of a spatially finite
profile whose last row is its edge (\(\mathcal{P} = 0\) at r_t),
the potential is the Kepler form \(M_t(1/r - 1/r_t)\) and the
density follows the edge law \(\rho \propto \mathcal{P}^q\) with
the stated edge_exponent; beyond r_t the potential is \(M_t/r\)
and the density zero. Inside the first row and, for a profile without
an edge, beyond the last, the interpolants continue as the power laws
of the end rows.

Parameters:

r (array, shape (n,)) – Radius, strictly increasing.

p_trunc (array, shape (n,)) – Total relative potential of the truncated model.

rho_trunc (array, shape (n_components, n)) – Density of each component.

mass_trunc (array, shape (n,)) – Total enclosed mass, in the unit of DoublePowerLaw.mass (the
Hernquist profile’s total is 1); 4 pi times it is the integral of
the density over the volume.

k_t (float) – Truncation energy.

r_t (float) – Truncation radius and total mass; infinite where the model is not
spatially finite.

mass_t (float) – Truncation radius and total mass; infinite where the model is not
spatially finite.

spatially_finite (bool) – Whether the density reaches zero at a finite radius with a finite
total mass. A spatially finite profile whose last row has
p_trunc == 0 carries its edge as that row, and then the row’s
density is zero and its radius is r_t.

source (DoublePowerLaw) – The analytic profile of the first component of the model: its scale
radius and its central potential are the internal units the arrays
are in.

source_anisotropy (Anisotropy) – The anisotropy of that component in the model the profile belongs
to. A component built on this profile (Method II) reads here what
its parent was.

model (str) – Identity string of the model the profile belongs to.

model_level (int or None) – The tier level of that model’s report (ValidationReport.level),
written by truncate, so that a component built on this profile
(Method II) takes it as its parents’ tier. None where it was not
recorded (a profile made otherwise, or read from a file written
before it was): read as level 0.

edge_exponent (tuple of float) – Exponent \(q\) of each component’s density at the edge of the
model, \(\rho \propto \mathcal{P}^q\); empty where the model
is not spatially finite and has no edge.

u_trunc (array, shape (n,)) – The central potential less the potential, p_trunc[0] + u_trunc[0]
less p_trunc, kept exact where p_trunc is close to it: near the
center p_trunc alone has lost the digits of the difference that the
DF’s singular center is read in. Empty where not computed.

central_deficit (tuple of tuple of float) – For each component, (D_0, D_1, …): the central auxiliary density
of the orbits the truncation removed as its Taylor series in the
depth u, D_0 - D_1 u + D_2 u^2 - … (D_0 to D_4 as made; a record
of D_0 and D_1 alone reads as the linear deficit). Empty where not
recorded.

override_r (float) – Radii between which the closed-form profile replaced the rows of
the solve; NaN where no row was replaced.

override_r_end (float) – Radii between which the closed-form profile replaced the rows of
the solve; NaN where no row was replaced.

df_k (array, shape (n_components, m)) – The DF table of the model the profile belongs to: the energies,
log10 F and its slope d log10 F / d ln K (NaN where not exact), as
truncate made them. A component built on this profile (Method II)
reads its sources from the integral of this DF. Empty where not
recorded.

df_log_f (array, shape (n_components, m)) – The DF table of the model the profile belongs to: the energies,
log10 F and its slope d log10 F / d ln K (NaN where not exact), as
truncate made them. A component built on this profile (Method II)
reads its sources from the integral of this DF. Empty where not
recorded.

df_slope (array, shape (n_components, m)) – The DF table of the model the profile belongs to: the energies,
log10 F and its slope d log10 F / d ln K (NaN where not exact), as
truncate made them. A component built on this profile (Method II)
reads its sources from the integral of this DF. Empty where not
recorded.

df_taylor (tuple of tuple of float) – For each component, the model’s Taylor edge (F_1, F_2, K_switch):
F = F_1 K + F_2 K^2 / 2 below K_switch. Empty where not recorded.

override_rows (int) – Number of rows replaced there.

override_rule (str) – What replaced them, "none" where nothing did.

origin (array of int8, shape (n,)) – Where each row comes from, a code of
pianistpy.df.truncation.ORIGINS (the main solve, the edge
continuation, the floor event, the fills, the closed-form outer rows,
the edge row): the profile’s checks read each row’s tolerance from it.
Empty where not recorded.

property has_edge_row: bool

Whether the last row is the edge of a spatially finite profile.

property r_table_max: float

the outer end of the table, which is
the edge of a spatially finite model.

Type:

The radius of the last row

property mass_at_r_table_max: float

mass_trunc at the last row.

potential_log_slope(r)

Return \(d\ln P / d\ln r\) at radii r, from the profile’s own
representation.

The slope is exact in the rows’ quantities: \(dP/dr = -M/r^2\)
(the Poisson equation in the profile’s unit), so
\(d\ln P/d\ln r = -M/(r P)\) with mass and potential read as
every consumer reads them. The knots of the representation are the
rows r; between two rows the slope is smooth.

Parameters:

r (Any)

Return type:

Any

potential_log_slope_derivative(r)

Return \(d(d\ln P/d\ln r)/dr\) at radii r, exact in the rows’
quantities.

With \(q = -M/(rP)\), \(dM/dr = r^2 \varrho\) (the total
density of the components) and \(dP/dr = -M/r^2\):
\(dq/dr = -(r^3 \varrho P - M P + M^2/r) / (r^2 P^2)\). Beyond the
edge the density is zero and the same form holds on the Kepler
potential.

Parameters:

r (Any)

Return type:

Any

radius(p)

Return the radii at which the potential takes the values p.

Values above the central potential are refused; a value of zero or
below is the truncation radius of a spatially finite profile.

Parameters:

p (Any)

Return type:

Any

to_dict()

Return what identifies the profile, as a plain dictionary.

The arrays are not part of it: the identity of the model determines
them, and a file holds them beside this record.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

# Runtime options

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/runtime

# Runtime options

Module pianistpy.runtime

Runtime options of the session: verbosity, timing and workers.

None of these changes a number, and none is part of the identity of a
result. Each is set once for the session, by a call or by an environment
variable, and no function of the package takes it as an argument.

class pianistpy.runtime.Timing(stages=<factory>, memory=<factory>)

Wall times of the stages of one computation, and the memory they reached.

Parameters:

stages (dict of str to float) – Seconds spent in each stage, in the order the stages first ran. A
stage that runs more than once accumulates.

memory (dict of str to int) – Peak resident memory of the process, in bytes, as it stood when each
stage last ended. The value never decreases from one stage to the
next: a stage raised the peak if its value exceeds the one before.

property total: float

Sum of the stage times, in seconds.

to_dict()

Return the stage times as a plain dictionary.

Return type:

dict[str, float]

pianistpy.runtime.allowed_cores()

Return the number of cores this process is allowed to use.

Inside a batch job the scheduler’s own statement of the job’s cores is
taken where it gives one; otherwise the cores the operating system lets
the process run on; otherwise the cores of the machine.

Return type:

int

pianistpy.runtime.card_memory()

Return the free and the total memory of the GPU JAX runs on, in
bytes, as the CUDA driver states them; None off a CUDA GPU.

The driver is asked in the device’s primary context, the one JAX uses,
so asking makes no context of its own. Its free memory counts what
every process holds on the GPU, a CUDA context included, which the
allocator’s own statistics do not.

Return type:

tuple[int, int] | None

pianistpy.runtime.configure_jax()

Set JAX as the package needs it: 64 bits, the platform and the
compilation cache.

Called once when the package is imported. The environment variable
PIANISTPY_PLATFORM names the platform (set_platform), and
PIANISTPY_COMPILATION_CACHE set to off leaves the cache off.

Return type:

None

pianistpy.runtime.default_compilation_cache()

Return the default folder of the compilation cache.

The environment variable PIANISTPY_COMPILATION_CACHE if it is set,
None if it is set to off (the cache is off), otherwise
~/.cache/pianistpy/jax.

Return type:

str | None

pianistpy.runtime.get_workers()

Return the number of workers the current setting resolves to.

Return type:

int

pianistpy.runtime.log_to_file(path, level='debug')

Write the messages of the enclosed block to a file as well.

Parameters:

path (path) – File to append to.

level ({"quiet", "info", "debug"}, optional) – Lowest level written to the file.

Return type:

Iterator[None]

pianistpy.runtime.peak_memory()

Return the largest resident memory this process has held, in bytes.

This is the memory of the host process. Memory held on a GPU is not
part of it.

Returns:

peak – The peak resident memory since the process started, or None where
the operating system does not report it.

Return type:

int or None

pianistpy.runtime.recent_messages()

Return the most recent messages of the package, oldest first.

The messages are kept whatever the verbosity, so that a quiet run that
fails can still say what it was doing.

Return type:

tuple[str, …]

pianistpy.runtime.platform()

Return the backend JAX runs on: "cpu", "gpu" or another.

Asking initializes the backend if it is not yet.

Return type:

str

pianistpy.runtime.set_compilation_cache(cache=True, max_size=None)

Turn the persistent compilation cache of JAX on or off.

With the cache on, the code compiled in one run is reused by the next,
which shortens every run after the first. It changes no number. The
cache is on by default, its folder unbounded in size, as JAX’s own is.

A bound costs time: JAX then takes a lock on the folder at every read
and write, and scans every entry at every write. Measured on a folder of
22,000 entries on a network file system, a test that takes 5.6 minutes
with no bound (4.3 to 5.2 minutes with eight runs at once on the folder,
as with the cache off) took 2 hours 8 minutes alone with a bound of
512 MiB.

Parameters:

cache (bool or path, optional) – True for the default folder (default_compilation_cache, or the
package’s own folder where the environment variable turns the cache
off), a path for another folder, False to turn the cache off.

max_size (int or None, optional) – Bound on the folder in bytes, above which JAX evicts the oldest
entries; None, the default, leaves the folder unbounded.

Returns:

folder – The folder in use, or None if the cache is off.

Return type:

str or None

pianistpy.runtime.set_platform(name)

Choose the hardware JAX runs on, before the first computation.

The CPU-only mode ("cpu") is first class: every function of the
package runs on it and gives the same numbers on every machine. It
changes no number on a machine without a GPU; on one with a GPU the
CPU and GPU results differ at rounding, as the provenance of each
file records (pianistpy.io.backend_provenance).

Parameters:

name ({"auto", "cpu", "gpu"}) – "auto" leaves JAX its own order (a GPU where one is usable);
"cpu" is the CPU-only mode; "gpu" asks for the CUDA backend
with the CPU behind it. Any other string is handed to JAX as its
own platform list (for example "rocm,cpu").

Return type:

None

Notes

JAX picks its backend at the first computation of the process and
keeps it: call this before any result is computed, or set the
environment variable PIANISTPY_PLATFORM before the package is
imported. A later call has no effect and is reported at info.

pianistpy.runtime.set_timing(enabled)

Switch the printing of stage times on or off.

The times are always measured and kept with the result. This switch
controls printing only and is independent of the verbosity. The
environment variable PIANISTPY_TIMING sets it at import.

Parameters:

enabled (bool)

Return type:

None

pianistpy.runtime.set_verbosity(level)

Set what the package prints for the rest of the session.

Parameters:

level ({"quiet", "info", "debug"}) – "quiet" shows warnings and errors only and is the default;
"info" adds one line per stage; "debug" adds the detail of
each stage.

Return type:

None

Notes

The verbosity never changes what is computed. The environment variable
PIANISTPY_VERBOSITY sets the level at import.

pianistpy.runtime.set_workers(value)

Set how many cores the package uses for parallel work.

Parameters:

value ({"auto", "full", "half"} or int) – "auto", the default, uses every allowed core inside a batch job
and half of them anywhere else; "full" every allowed core;
"half" half of them; an integer exactly that many.

Return type:

None

Notes

The number of workers never changes a number: a result is the same, to
the bit, for any value. The environment variable PIANISTPY_WORKERS
sets the value at import.

pianistpy.runtime.timed(stage)

Time one stage and announce it.

Parameters:

stage (str) – Name of the stage, from the fixed list of its computation.

Return type:

Iterator[None]

pianistpy.runtime.timing_enabled()

Return whether stage times are printed.

Return type:

bool

pianistpy.runtime.timing_record()

Yields:

timing (Timing) – The record that every timed stage of the block adds to.

Return type:

Iterator[Timing]

pianistpy.runtime.workers_explicit()

Whether the workers were set to an exact number (set_workers).

Return type:

bool

# Settings

Module pianistpy.settings

Numerical settings: the tested tiers and expert overrides.

class pianistpy.settings.Field(default, doc, quick=None)

One numerical setting: its value in each tier and what it controls.

Parameters:

doc (str) – What the field controls.

quick (bool, int, float or str, optional) – Value in the quick tier. If omitted, the quick tier keeps the default
value: a cheaper value enters only once it has passed the tests.

value(tier)

Return the value of the field in a tier.

Parameters:

tier (str)

Return type:

Any

class pianistpy.settings.Settings(quick=False, write_anyway=False, **overrides)

Numerical settings of a computation.

A tier is a complete set of numerical settings that has been run through
the test battery and for which the package states the accuracy it
delivers. An expert may override single fields; the result then records
that it was not made with a tested tier and names the fields that differ.

Parameters:

quick (bool, optional) – Use the quick tier instead of the default tier.

write_anyway (bool, optional) – Return a result whose own check lies beyond the hard limit instead of
refusing it. The result carries the check’s verdict in its validation
report (tier "refused") and an AccuracyWarning is issued in
place of the refusal. For debugging a case the package cannot serve
at its stated accuracy; off by default. A physically invalid model
is refused regardless.

**overrides (mapping) – One mapping per group (inversion, truncation, sampling,
observables, losvd) of the fields to change within that group.

Variables:

tier (str) – Name of the tier the settings start from.

write_anyway (bool) – Whether a result beyond the hard limit is returned instead of refused.

overrides (mapping) – The fields changed from the tier, by group. Read only.

Examples

```
>>> Settings().tier
'default'
>>> Settings(quick=True).is_tested_tier
True
>>> Settings(inversion={"n_nodes": 256}).is_tested_tier
False
>>> Settings(inversion={"n_nodes": 256}).inversion["n_nodes"]
256
>>> Settings().truncation["ode_rtol"]
1e-11

```

property tier: str

Name of the tier the settings start from.

property write_anyway: bool

Whether a result beyond the hard limit is returned instead of refused.

property overrides: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]

The fields changed from the tier, by group.

property is_tested_tier: bool

Whether the settings are a tested tier with no field changed.

Return the value of every field of one group.

Parameters:

name (str) – One of the groups inversion, truncation, sampling,
observables and losvd.

Returns:

values – The fields of the group with the values of the tier, each
replaced by its override where one was given. Read only.

Return type:

mapping

property inversion: Mapping[str, Any]

Settings of the inversion.

property truncation: Mapping[str, Any]

Settings of the truncation.

property sampling: Mapping[str, Any]

Settings of the particle sampling.

property observables: Mapping[str, Any]

Settings of the observables.

property losvd: Mapping[str, Any]

The fields of the LOSVD table and the aperture LOSVD.

Return type:

# Superposition

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/superposition

# Superposition

Module pianistpy.superposition

Linear superposition of models that share one density.

pianistpy.superposition.mixture(weights, values, xp=np)

Return the weighted sum of per-component values, the weights normalized.

The one way a superposed model combines its components: a density, a
moment or a table read per component. Linear in the values, and in the
weights up to their normalization; with xp=jax.numpy the weights may
be traced, so a quantity of the mixture is differentiable in them.

Parameters:

weights (array-like, shape (n_components,)) – Positive weights; normalized here.

values (array-like, shape (n_components, ...)) – The value of each component.

xp (module, optional) – numpy, or jax.numpy for traced weights.

Returns:

value

Return type:

array, shape (…)

pianistpy.superposition.moments(model, r, n_nodes=None)

Return the second moments of a superposed model at radii r.

Parameters:

model (Model) – A superposed model (superpose), its components sharing one density.

r (array-like, shape (n,)) – Radii, in internal units.

n_nodes (int, optional) – Gauss-Legendre nodes of each component’s Jeans integral; the model’s
observables.n_jeans_nodes if omitted.

Returns:

moments – sigma_r2 and sigma_t2 of the mixture, beta_sigma its
anisotropy, and sigma_r2_components and beta_components (one
row per component), with the shape of r.

Return type:

dict

Notes

Each component’s radial dispersion is the Jeans integral of its
auxiliary density on the shared profile (radial_dispersion, the
Gauss-Legendre rule in ln(1 - K / P_0)); its components share the density,
so the moments of the mixture are the weighted sums
\(\sigma_r^2 = \sum_k w_k\sigma_{r,k}^2\),
\(\sigma_t^2 = 2\sum_k w_k(1-\beta_k)\sigma_{r,k}^2\) and
\(\beta_\sigma = 1 - \sigma_t^2 / (2\sigma_r^2)\).

References

Chiang+(2026d), Eqs. (B42), (B43) [eqn:linearity_2, eqn:linearity_beta_1] and
eqn:beta_sigma_sup.

pianistpy.superposition.superpose(members)

Return the superposition of models that share one truncated pair.

Parameters:

members (mapping of Model to float) – Two or more models of one component each, every one built on the same
truncated profile (Method II children of one truncated parent), with
their weights. The weights must be positive; they are normalized to
sum to one, with a warning where they did not.

Returns:

model – One component per member, in the order given: the member’s component
with its mass the weight relative to the first member’s; its DF table
on its own energy grid (DfTable carries one grid per component); the
shared profile with the density split by weight; the members’ checks,
each at its worst over the members.

Return type:

Model

Raises:

InputError – If fewer than two members are given, a weight is not positive and
    finite, a member is not a single Method II component on a truncated
    profile, the members are built on different profiles, or their
    settings or units differ.

     On this page

# Units

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/units

# Units

Module pianistpy.units

Conversion from internal units to model and physical units.

class pianistpy.units.UnitFactors(rho_norm, mass_q, model_v, model_mass, model_rho, model_p, physical_r_pc=None, physical_v_kms=None, physical_mass_msun=None, physical_rho_msun_pc3=None, physical_p_kms2=None, physical_rho_0_msun_pc3=None)

Factors that convert internal units to model and to physical units.

A quantity in internal units is multiplied by the factor to obtain it in
the target units. The model units have \(G = M_0 = r_0 = 1\), with
\(M_0\) the mass inside the radius concentration times
\(r_0\).

Parameters:

rho_norm (float) – Normalization \(C\) of the density profile.

mass_q (float) – \(q = \mathcal{M}(c)/C\), the mass inside the concentration
radius in units of \(4\pi\rho_0 r_0^3\).

model_v (float) – Factors to the model units, for a speed, a mass, a density and a
potential.

model_mass (float) – Factors to the model units, for a speed, a mass, a density and a
potential.

model_rho (float) – Factors to the model units, for a speed, a mass, a density and a
potential.

model_p (float) – Factors to the model units, for a speed, a mass, a density and a
potential.

physical_r_pc (float or None) – Factors to parsecs, kilometers per second and solar masses.

physical_v_kms (float or None) – Factors to parsecs, kilometers per second and solar masses.

physical_mass_msun (float or None) – Factors to parsecs, kilometers per second and solar masses.

physical_rho_msun_pc3 (float or None) – Factors to solar masses per cubic parsec, and to the square of
kilometers per second.

physical_p_kms2 (float or None) – Factors to solar masses per cubic parsec, and to the square of
kilometers per second.

physical_rho_0_msun_pc3 (float or None) – The scale density \(\rho_0\) in solar masses per cubic parsec.

Notes

The physical factors are None unless both physical scales were given to
unit_factors.

class pianistpy.units.Units(system='internal', concentration=None, mass_0_msun=None, r_0_pc=None)

The unit system of a result and the scales that define it.

Parameters:

system ({"internal", "model", "physical"}) – "internal": \(G = \rho_0/C = r_0 = 1\). "model":
\(G = M_0 = r_0 = 1\). "physical": Astropy quantities.

concentration (float, optional) – Concentration \(c\) that defines \(M_0\) as the mass inside
\(c\,r_0\). Needed by the model and the physical systems.

mass_0_msun (float, optional) – \(M_0\) in solar masses. Needed by the physical system.

r_0_pc (float, optional) – Scale radius \(r_0\) in parsecs. Needed by the physical system.

Examples

```
>>> Units().system
'internal'
>>> Units.build("model", concentration=10.0).concentration
10.0

```

classmethod build(system, concentration=None, mass_0=None, r_0=None, r_vir=None)

Return the units of a system from the scales a user gives.

Parameters:

system ({"internal", "model", "physical"}) – The target system.

concentration (float, optional) – Concentration that defines \(M_0\).

mass_0 (float or astropy Quantity, optional) – \(M_0\); a float is in solar masses.

r_0 (float or astropy Quantity, optional) – The scale radius, or the radius \(c\,r_0\) in its place; a
float is in parsecs. One of the two for the physical system.

r_vir (float or astropy Quantity, optional) – The scale radius, or the radius \(c\,r_0\) in its place; a
float is in parsecs. One of the two for the physical system.

Returns:

units

Return type:

Units

factors(profile)

Return the conversion factors of these units for a density profile.

Parameters:

profile (DoublePowerLaw)

Return type:

UnitFactors

convert(kind, value, profile)

Return a quantity in internal units in the units of this object.

Parameters:

kind ({"length", "velocity", "mass", "density", "potential"}) – What the quantity is.

value (array-like) – The quantity, in internal units.

profile (DoublePowerLaw) – The density profile that fixes the normalization.

Returns:

converted – A plain array for the internal and the model systems, an Astropy
quantity for the physical system.

Return type:

array or astropy Quantity

to_dict()

Return the units as a plain dictionary.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

classmethod from_dict(record)

Build the units from their dictionary form; internal if absent.

Parameters:

record (Mapping[str, Any] | None)

Return type:

Units

pianistpy.units.unit_factors(profile, concentration, mass_0_msun=None, r_0_pc=None)

Return the conversion factors of a profile.

Parameters:

profile (DoublePowerLaw) – The density profile, which fixes the normalization \(C\).

concentration (float) – Radius, in units of the scale radius \(r_0\), inside which the
mass \(M_0\) is defined. Positive.

mass_0_msun (float, optional) – \(M_0\) in solar masses.

r_0_pc (float, optional) – Scale radius \(r_0\) in parsecs.

Returns:

factors – The model-unit factors, and the physical factors if both mass_0_msun
and r_0_pc are given.

Return type:

UnitFactors

Notes

With \(\rho_{\rm w} = \rho_0/C\) the internal units are
\(M_{\rm W} = 4\pi\rho_{\rm w} r_0^3\) for mass and
\(v_{\rm W} = \sqrt{4\pi G\rho_{\rm w} r_0^2}\) for speed, and
\(M_0 = 4\pi\rho_0 r_0^3\,q\). Hence a speed is multiplied by
\((C q)^{-1/2}\), a mass and a potential by \((C q)^{-1}\), and a
density by \((4\pi C q)^{-1}\) to reach the model units.

References

Chiang+(2026d), Section on units (labels ssec:Units, eqn:M_nor_1).

Examples

```
>>> factors = unit_factors(DoublePowerLaw.nfw(), concentration=10.0)
>>> factors.rho_norm
1.0
>>> round(factors.mass_q, 12) == round(math.log(11.0) - 10.0 / 11.0, 12)
True

```

     On this page

# Validation

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/validation

# Validation

Module pianistpy.validation

Accuracy tiers and the validation report of a result.

class pianistpy.validation.Check(error, where=None, reason=None, source=None, excluded=None)

One check of a result: what was measured and where.

Parameters:

error (float) – The relative error the check measured.

where (float, optional) – The place of the largest error, in the variable the check runs over
(a radius or an energy). Absent where that has no meaning.

reason (str, optional) – Why the check was not judged, where it was not: such a check has no
error (NaN), its tier reads "not judged", and the result’s tier
is the worst of the checks that were.

source (str, optional) – Where a judged check read its input from another source than its
own, what it read and why; the error and the tier are as measured.

excluded (str, optional) – Where a judged check leaves part of its input unjudged, which part
and why; the error and the tier are those of the rest.

property level: int

Tier of the error, as returned by tier_level; 0 for a check not
judged, which leaves the result’s tier to the others.

property tier: str

Name of the tier of the error, or "not judged".

class pianistpy.validation.ValidationReport(keys, checks, parents_level=0)

The validation report of one result.

The report has a fixed set of keys for each kind of result and one
Check per key. It is not a log: nothing is appended to it, and a
derived result holds its own checks and the worst tier of its parents,
never a copy of their reports.

Parameters:

keys (tuple of str) – The keys this kind of result reports, in order.

checks (mapping of str to Check) – One check per key.

parents_level (int, optional) – Worst tier among the parents of the result.

property level: int

Worst tier of the result’s own checks and of its parents.

property tier: str

Name of the worst tier.

classmethod from_dict(record, key_sets=None)

Build the report from its dictionary form.

Parameters:

record (mapping) – The report as to_dict writes it.

key_sets (sequence of tuple of str, optional) – The key sets a report of this kind of result has. Given, a check
no set holds is refused by name, and the report is read against
the smallest set that holds all its checks: a check of that set
the record lacks (a file written before the check was made) is
read as not judged, with that reason.

Raises:

ResultError – If a check of the record is in none of the key sets, or no one
    set holds all its checks.

Return type:

ValidationReport

to_dict()

Return the report as a plain dictionary, in the order of its keys.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

pianistpy.validation.announce(what, report, detail)

Say that a result lies above the goal; silent within it.

The one channel for every block: the package’s log (the pianistpy
logger, printed by default) and Python’s own warnings, as an
AccuracyWarning, so that a user can silence or escalate it with the
standard filter. Nothing is said within the goal; beyond the hard limit
the result is refused by its stage, not announced here.

Parameters:

what (str) – The result, named: "The sampler of 'nfw'".

report (ValidationReport) – Its report.

detail (str) – The checks above the goal with their errors and where they occur.

Return type:

None

pianistpy.validation.refuse_unless_asked(what, report, settings)

Refuse a result beyond the hard limit as the input of another.

A result whose report reads "refused" exists only because it was asked
for anyway (Settings(write_anyway=True)) or was read from a file that
holds one. It is consumed only under the same request: a sampler, a table
or a projection built on it carries its tier and says so.

Parameters:

what (str) – The input, named: "The model 'nfw'".

report (ValidationReport) – Its report.

settings (Settings) – The settings of the result being built from it.

Raises:

AccuracyError – If the report’s tier is "refused" and the settings do not ask for
    the result anyway.

Return type:

None

pianistpy.validation.tier_level(error)

Return the tier of a relative error.

Parameters:

error (float) – Relative error, non-negative. A value that is not a number counts as
beyond the hard limit.

Returns:

level – 0 within the goal, 1 within the ceiling, 2 within the hard limit,
3 beyond it.

Return type:

int

Examples

```
>>> [tier_level(e) for e in (1e-7, 1e-5, 1e-3, 1e-1, float("nan"))]
[0, 1, 2, 3, 3]

```

# Technical notes

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/notes

# Technical notes

This technical document details the analytical and numerical treatments implemented in PIANISTpy, building upon the high-level overviews provided in the initial code release paper of Chiang, van den Bosch and Schive (2026d), cited throughout as Chiang+(2026d). Here, we follow and routinely refer to the notations, equations, and results of that paper. This document is organized by the objects of the pipeline, from upstream to downstream, and each object-specific section first treats the analytical theory (whenever applicable) and then the accompanying numerical implementations. Section T:0 states the conventions and notations used; we then discuss the input potential-density models (Section T:1), the distribution function (Section T:2), the truncation (Section T:3), the linear superposition of components (Section T:4), the particle sampling (Section T:5), the velocity profiles and projections (Section T:6), and the JAX-based gradients (Section T:7). Section T:8 documents the accuracy and validation tests and related information.

This is version 7 of the notes. Their numbers carry the prefix T: (sections T:2.3, equations (T:2.4), tables T:2.1); the package’s docstrings cite them in the form the API reference states. The notes are also published as a PDF with each release; the link is added with ver. 1.0.0.

# Settings tables

# Settings tables

Every numerical setting of the package is a declared field of one group, with its value in each tested tier and
one line on what it controls. The tables below are generated from the package’s own declaration at every build
of this manual, so they cannot lag the code. The settings container is pianistpy.Settings; a stage reads
its group and nothing else; an override of an undeclared field, of the wrong type or not positive is refused.

# Names and paper symbols

Source: https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/symbols

# Names and paper symbols

The package’s names follow the notation of Chiang+(2026d): a quantity that has a symbol there or in the technical notes
is named <family>_<symbol>, the family saying what kind of quantity it is and the rest being that symbol
or subscript in lower case. A truncated quantity (hatted in Chiang+(2026d)) takes the suffix _trunc, the
untruncated one the bare name. Every docstring gives that symbol beside the name the first time it
describes it.

Family

Prefix

Names

Paper

density and its parameters

rho_

rho, rho_aux, rho_alpha, rho_beta, rho_gamma, rho_norm

\(\varrho\), \(\varrho_{\rm aux}\), \((\alpha, \beta, \gamma)\), \(C\)

anisotropy

beta_

beta_c, beta_sigma, beta_sup

\(\beta_{\rm c}\), \(\beta_\sigma\), \(\beta_{\rm sup}\)

radii

r_

r, r_a, r_t, r_2d, r_off, r_ape

\(R\), \(R_{\rm a}\), \(R_{\rm t}\), \(R_{\rm 2D}\), \(R_{\rm off}\), \(R_{\rm ape}\)

relative potential

p_

p, p_0

\(P\), \(P_0\)

energy-like variables

k_, q_

k, k_t, q, q_min, q_0

\(\mathcal{K}\), \(\mathcal{K}_{\rm t}\), \(\mathcal{Q}\), \(\mathcal{Q}_{\rm min}\), \(\mathcal{Q}_0\)

distribution function

df_

df, df_k

\(F\), \(F_\mathcal{K}\)

mass

mass_

mass, mass_t, mass_vir

\(\mathcal{M}\), \(M_{\rm t}\), \(M_{\rm vir}\)

order of the inversion

order_

order_m, order_n

\((m, n)\)

velocities and dispersions

v_, sigma_

v_r, v_t, v_los, v_esc, sigma_r, sigma_t, sigma_los

\(V_{\rm r}\), \(V_{\rm t}\), \(V_{\rm los}\), \(V_{\rm esc}\), \(\sigma_{\rm r}\), \(\sigma_{\rm t}\), \(\sigma_{\rm los}\)

probability densities

pdf_

pdf_x, pdf_phi

\(p_x\), \(p_\varphi\)

Where the letter of Chiang+(2026d) cannot be used, a word is fixed: the normalization \(C\) of the density is
rho_norm (rho_c would read as a central density), and the concentration \(c\) is concentration.
The letter c alone is never a name; as a subscript it means central (beta_c). The quantities of the
truncated model carry the suffix: p_trunc, df_trunc, rho_trunc, mass_trunc.

## Derived names

What

Form

Example

logarithm of a quantity

ln_, log10_ prefix

ln_r, log10_df

derivative

d<y>_d<x>, the order as a digit

drho_dp, d2rho_dp2

count

n_ prefix

n_nodes, n_rows

index

i_ prefix

i_split

quadrature nodes and weights

_nodes, _weights suffix

k_nodes, k_weights

tabulated values on a grid

_grid suffix

r_grid, df_grid

boolean

is_, has_ prefix

is_truncated, has_tail

The three unit systems are named internal (the dimensionless normalization of Widrow 2000, in which the
scale radius and the central potential of the untruncated profile are 1), model (\(G = M_0 = r_0 = 1\))
and physical (through Astropy); see Units.
